title.zh: 卷四百二十二 列傳第一百八十一 林勳 劉才邵 許忻 應孟明 曾三聘 徐僑 度正 程珌 牛大年 陳仲微 梁成大 李知孝
title.en: Volume 422 Biographies 181: Lin Xun, Liu Cai Shao, Xu Xin, Ying Mengming, Ceng Sanpin, Xu Qiao, Du Zheng, Cheng Bi, Niu Danian, Chen Zhongwei, Liang Chengda, Li Zhixiao
title.raw: 卷四百二十二 列傳第一百八十一 林勳 劉才邵 許忻 應孟明 曾三聘 徐僑 度正 程珌 牛大年 陳仲微 梁成大 李知孝 Volume 422 Biographies 181: Lin Xun, Liu Cai Shao, Xu Xin, Ying Mengming, Ceng Sanpin, Xu Qiao, Du Zheng, Cheng Bi, Niu Danian, Chen Zhongwei, Liang Chengda, Li Zhixiao

sentences.zh: 林勛劉才邵許忻應孟明曾三聘徐僑度正程必牛大年陳仲微梁成大李知孝

translations.literal: Lin Xun, Liu Caishao, Xu Xin, Ying Mengming, Zeng Sanpin, Xu Qiao, Du Zheng, Cheng Bi, Niu Danian, Chen Zhongwei, Liang Chengda, Li Zhixiao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xun, Liu Caishao, Xu Xin, Ying Mengming, Zeng Sanpin, Xu Qiao, Du Zheng, Cheng Bi, Niu Danian, Chen Zhongwei, Liang Chengda, and Li Zhixiao.

sentences.zh: 林勛，賀州人。

translations.literal: Lin Xun was a man of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Xun was a native of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 政和五年進士，為廣州教授。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenghe he became a jinshi and served as instructor at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Zhenghe reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed instructor at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年八月，獻《本政書》十三篇，言：“國家兵農之政，率因唐末之故。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Jianyan he submitted thirteen chapters of the Ben Zheng Shu, saying: "The state's policies for army and agriculture largely follow conditions at the end of the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Jianyan he presented thirteen chapters of his Fundamental Governance, stating: "The state's military and agricultural policies largely perpetuate the disorders of late Tang.

sentences.zh: 今農貧而多失職，兵驕而不可用，是以饑民竄卒，類為盜賊。

translations.literal: Now farmers are poor and many lose their livelihoods; soldiers are arrogant and cannot be used—thus hungry people and idle soldiers mostly become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Today the peasants are impoverished and many lack steady employment, while the troops are insubordinate and unfit for service; hungry civilians and idle soldiers alike drift into banditry.

sentences.zh: 宜仿古井田之制，使民一夫占田五十畝，其有羨田之家，毋得市田，其無田與遊惰末作者，皆驅之使為隸農，以耕田之羨者，而雜紐錢谷，以為十一之稅。

translations.literal: One should imitate the ancient well-field system, having each man occupy fifty mu; households with surplus land must not buy more fields; those without land and idle people in marginal trades should all be driven to serve as dependent farmers, cultivating others' surplus fields, while assorted taxes on grain and money should serve as the one-tenth tax.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed reviving the ancient well-field system: each household head would hold fifty mu; families with surplus land could not purchase more; landless men and idle hangers-on in marginal trades would be compelled to work as tenant farmers on others' surplus acreage, with miscellaneous levies on grain and cash consolidated into a single tithe.

sentences.zh: 宋二稅之數，視唐增至七倍。

translations.literal: The Song's two-tax levies were seven times what they had been under the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song, the burden of the two-tax system had grown to seven times its Tang level.

sentences.zh: 今本政之制，每十六夫為一井，提封百里，為三千四百井，率稅米五萬一千斛、錢萬二千緡；

translations.literal: Under the present system of fundamental governance, every sixteen householders form one 'well'; within a hundred-li district there are 3,400 wells, yielding in tax 51,000 hu of grain and 12,000 strings of cash;
translations.idiomatic: Under his new scheme, sixteen householders would form one well-field unit; a district of a hundred li would contain 3,400 such units, yielding roughly 51,000 hu of grain and 12,000 strings of cash in tax;

sentences.zh: 每井賦二兵、馬一匹，率為兵六千八百人、馬三千四百匹，歲取五之一以為上番之額，以給征役。

translations.literal: Each well supplies two soldiers and one horse, totalling 6,800 soldiers and 3,400 horses; each year one-fifth is taken as the quota for rotation on campaign, to supply military service.
translations.idiomatic: each unit would furnish two soldiers and one horse—6,800 troops and 3,400 mounts in all—with one-fifth levied annually as the rotating quota for active campaigning.

sentences.zh: 無事則又分為四番，以直官府，以給守衛。

translations.literal: When there is no campaigning they are further divided into four rotations to staff government offices and provide guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime the force would be split into four reliefs to man government offices and garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 是民凡三十五年而役使一遍也。

translations.literal: Thus the common people complete one full cycle of service only every thirty-five years.
translations.idiomatic: Thus an ordinary farmer would complete only one full cycle of compulsory service every thirty-five years.

sentences.zh: 悉上則歲食米萬九千餘斛，錢三千六百餘緡，無事則減四分之三，皆以一同之租稅供之。

translations.literal: When fully deployed, grain consumption is over 19,000 hu and cash over 3,600 strings per year; when idle, this is reduced by three-quarters—all supplied from the same uniform land tax.
translations.idiomatic: At full mobilization the district would consume over 19,000 hu of grain and more than 3,600 strings of cash yearly; in quiet times that outlay would drop by three-quarters—all borne by a single, uniform land tax.

sentences.zh: 匹婦之貢，絹三尺，綿一兩。

translations.literal: Each married woman's tribute: three chi of silk, one liang of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Each married woman would owe three feet of silk and one ounce of cotton floss.

sentences.zh: 百里之縣，歲收絹四千餘匹，綿三千四百斤。

translations.literal: A hundred-li county collects over 4,000 bolts of silk and 3,400 jin of cotton per year.
translations.idiomatic: A county of a hundred li would thus collect more than four thousand bolts of silk and 3,400 jin of cotton annually.

sentences.zh: 非蠶鄉則布六尺、麻二兩，所收視絹綿率倍之。

translations.literal: In non-sericulture districts, six chi of cloth and two liang of hemp; collections are roughly double those of silk and cotton.
translations.idiomatic: In districts without sericulture, six feet of cloth and two ounces of hemp would be substituted, with collections roughly double the silk and cotton totals.

sentences.zh: 行之十年，則民之口算，官之酒酤，與凡茶、鹽、香、礬之榷，皆可弛以予民。”

translations.literal: After ten years of implementation, household head taxes, government wine monopolies, and all levies on tea, salt, incense, and alum could be abolished and returned to the people."
translations.idiomatic: After a decade of operation, poll taxes, the state wine monopoly, and every excise on tea, salt, incense, and alum could be lifted and returned to the people."

sentences.zh: 其說甚備。

translations.literal: His exposition was very thorough.
translations.idiomatic: His argument was set forth in full detail.

sentences.zh: 書奏，以勛為桂州節度掌書記。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Lin was appointed clerk to the military governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, Lin was appointed secretary to the military commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 其後，勛又獻《比較書》二篇，大略謂：“桂州地東西六百里，南北五百里，以古尺計之，為方百里之國四十，當墾田二百二十五萬二千八百頃，有田夫二百四萬八千，出米二十四萬八千斛，祿卿大夫以下四千人，祿兵三十萬人。

translations.literal: Later Lin again submitted two chapters of the Bi Jiao Shu, broadly stating: "The territory of Guizhou extends six hundred li east-west and five hundred li north-south; measured by the ancient foot, this equals forty states of a hundred li square each, which should yield 2,252,800 qing of arable land, 2,048,000 field laborers, 248,000 hu of grain output, stipends for four thousand from grandee down, and provisions for three hundred thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted two chapters of a Comparative Study, arguing in substance that "Guizhou's domain—six hundred li east to west and five hundred north to south—would equal forty ideal states of a hundred li square under the ancient measure, capable of supporting 2,252,800 qing under the plow, 2,048,000 cultivators, 248,000 hu of grain, stipends for four thousand officials from grandee downward, and rations for three hundred thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 今桂州墾田約萬四十二頃，丁二十一萬六千六百一十五，稅錢萬五千餘緡，苗米五萬二百斛有奇，州縣官不滿百員，官兵五千一百人。

translations.literal: Today Guizhou has only about 10,420 qing under cultivation, 216,615 adult males, over 15,000 strings in tax money, over 50,200 hu of grain levy, fewer than a hundred county and prefectural officials, and 5,100 officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In reality Guizhou had only about 10,420 qing under cultivation, 216,615 registered males, a little over 15,000 strings in tax money, somewhat more than 50,200 hu of grain levy, fewer than a hundred prefectural and county officials, and 5,100 troops.

sentences.zh: 蓋土地荒蕪而遊手末作之人眾，是以地利多遺，財用不足，皆本政不修之故。”

translations.literal: The land lies fallow while idle hands in marginal trades are numerous; thus much productive capacity is lost and revenues insufficient—all because fundamental governance has not been put in order."
translations.idiomatic: The land lay largely fallow while idlers in marginal trades were numerous; productive capacity went untapped and revenues fell short—all because fundamental governance had not been restored."

sentences.zh: 朱熹甚愛其書。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi greatly admired his book.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi admired the work deeply.

sentences.zh: 東陽陳亮曰：“勛為此書，考古驗今，思慮周密，可謂勤矣。

translations.literal: Chen Liang of Dongyang said: "For Lin to write this book, examining antiquity and testing the present, his thought was so thorough one may call him diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Liang of Dongyang wrote: "In composing this book Lin examined antiquity and tested the present; his thinking is so thorough that one must call him diligent.

sentences.zh: 世之為井地之學者，孰有加於勛者乎？

translations.literal: Among those in the world who study the well-field system, who surpasses Lin?
translations.idiomatic: Among scholars of the well-field system in our age, who surpasses Lin?

sentences.zh: 要必有英雄特起之君，用於一變之後，成順致利，則民不駭而可以善其後矣。”

translations.literal: But there must surely be a ruler who rises above the common run, who after one great transformation applies it so that advantage follows naturally—then the people will not be alarmed and the aftermath can be managed well.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it will require a ruler of heroic stature, who after one decisive transformation applies the scheme so that benefit follows naturally—only then will the people not be alarmed and the consequences can be managed well."

sentences.zh: 劉才邵，字美中，吉州廬陵人。

translations.literal: Liu Caishao, courtesy name Meizhong, was a man of Luling in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Caishao, whose courtesy name was Meizhong, was a native of Luling in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 其上世鶚，太宗召見，未及用而卒。

translations.literal: His ancestor He in an earlier generation was summoned by Taizong but died before he could be employed.
translations.idiomatic: His forebear He had been summoned to audience by Emperor Taizong but died before he could take office.

sentences.zh: 嘗憤五季文辭卑弱，仿楊雄《法言》，著《法語》八十一篇行於世。

translations.literal: He had resented the weakness of Five Dynasties literary style and, imitating Yang Xiong's Fayan, composed eighty-one chapters of Fayu circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had deplored the debased style of Five Dynasties writing and, imitating Yang Xiong's Exemplary Sayings, composed eighty-one chapters of his own Exemplary Sayings, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 才邵以大觀二年上舍釋褐，為贛、汝二州教授，復為湖北提舉學事管幹文字。

translations.literal: Caishao passed the upper-house examination in the second year of Daguan, entered office, served as instructor in Gan and Ru prefectures, and again as clerical officer for the Hubei education intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Caishao graduated from the Imperial University in the second year of Daguan and entered service as instructor in Gan and Ru prefectures, then as clerical officer under the Hubei education intendant.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年，中宏詞科，遷司農寺丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuanhe he passed the macro-words examination and was promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuanhe he passed the macro-words examination and was appointed vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，遷校書郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang he was promoted to proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang he was promoted to proofreader in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，以親老歸侍，居閑十年。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, he returned home to attend his aged parents and lived in retirement for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong acceded, he returned home to care for his aging parents and lived in retirement for ten years.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞廖剛薦之，召見，遷秘書丞，歷駕部員外郎，遷吏部員外郎，典侍右選事。

translations.literal: Vice censor-in-chief Liao Gang recommended him; summoned to audience, he was made secretary director, then successively outer court director in the Transport Bureau and the Ministry of Personnel, in charge of selection for the eastern office of attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Vice censor-in-chief Liao Gang recommended him; summoned to audience, he was made secretary director, then served successively as outer court director in the Transport Bureau and the Ministry of Personnel, overseeing appointments in the eastern selection office for attendants.

sentences.zh: 先是，宗室註宮觀、嶽廟，例須赴部，遠者或難於行。

translations.literal: Previously, when clan members registered for palace temples and mountain shrines, they had to appear at the ministry in person, which those far away sometimes found hard to do.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when imperial clansmen registered for sinecures at palace temples and mountain shrines, they were required to appear in person at the ministry—a hardship for those posted far away.

sentences.zh: 才邵言許經所屬以聞於部，依條註擬，行之而便。

translations.literal: Caishao proposed allowing them to report through their local office to the ministry, which would register according to regulations—this was put into practice and proved convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Caishao proposed allowing them to report through their local jurisdiction to the ministry, which would register them according to regulation; the practice was adopted and proved convenient.

sentences.zh: 遷軍器監，既而遷起居舍人，未幾，為中書舍人兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Directorate of Armaments, then promoted to attendant recorder, and soon after made drafting academician of the Secretariat with acting charge of the academy institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Directorate of Armaments, then promoted to attendant recorder; before long he became drafting academician of the Secretariat with acting charge of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝稱其能文，時宰忌之，出知漳州。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his literary ability, but the chief minister envied him and had him sent out as prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his literary gifts, but the chief minister resented him and had him transferred out as prefect of Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 即城東開渠十有四，為閘與鬥門以瀦匯決，溉田數千畝。

translations.literal: East of the city he opened fourteen canals, installing sluices and floodgates to store and release water, irrigating several thousand mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city he excavated fourteen canals, installing sluices and floodgates to store and release water, irrigating several thousand mu of farmland.

sentences.zh: 民甚德之。

translations.literal: The people greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The people were deeply grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 兩奉祠。

translations.literal: He twice received palace-temple appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He twice held temple sinecures.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十五年，召拜工部侍郎兼直學士院，尋權吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Shaoxing he was summoned and appointed vice minister of Works with concurrent academy academician, soon acting minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Shaoxing he was recalled and appointed vice minister of Works with concurrent Hanlin academician, and soon after served as acting minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以疾請祠，加顯謨閣直學士。

translations.literal: He requested a temple appointment on grounds of illness and was given the additional title of academician of the Xianmo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a temple appointment on grounds of illness and was granted the additional title of academician of the Xianmo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈通奉大夫。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee for Propagating Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee for Propagating Merit.

sentences.zh: 才邵氣和貌恭，方權臣用事之時，雍容遜避，以保名節。

translations.literal: Caishao was mild in bearing and respectful in manner; when powerful ministers held sway, he remained at ease and yielded ground to preserve his reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Caishao was mild in temperament and respectful in bearing; when powerful ministers held sway, he met them with composed deference and withdrew when he must, preserving his reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 所著《檆溪居士集》行世。

translations.literal: His collected works Sansi Jushi ji circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works, the Sansi Hermit's Writings, circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 許忻，拱州人。

translations.literal: Xu Xin was a man of Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xin was a native of Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年進士，高宗時，為吏部員外郎，有旨引見。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the third year of Xuanhe; under Gaozong he was outer vice director of Personnel and received an imperial order for audience.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Xuanhe; under Emperor Gaozong he served as outer vice director of the Ministry of Personnel and received an imperial summons to audience.

sentences.zh: 是時，金國使人張通古在館，忻上疏極論和議不便，曰：

translations.literal: At that time the Jin envoy Zhang Tonggu was lodged at the guest house; Xin memorialized at length that peace talks were ill-advised, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jin envoy Zhang Tonggu was lodged in the guest residence; Xin submitted a memorial arguing forcefully that peace negotiations were inadvisable, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣兩蒙召見，擢置文館，今茲復降睿旨引對。

translations.literal: Your servant has twice been summoned to audience and placed in the literary halls; now again Your Majesty has graciously ordered another interview.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has twice been summoned to audience and placed among the literary officers; now Your Majesty has again graciously ordered me to attend for counsel.

sentences.zh: 今見陛下於多故之時，欲采千慮一得之說以廣聰明，是臣圖報萬分之秋也，故敢竭愚而效忠。

translations.literal: Now that I see Your Majesty in troubled times wishing to gather counsel however slender, to broaden your discernment—this is the season when your servant might repay you in the slightest measure; therefore I dare exhaust my dull wit in loyal service.
translations.idiomatic: I see Your Majesty in these troubled times seeking even the slenderest counsel to sharpen your judgment; this is the moment when your servant might repay you in the smallest measure, and so I dare offer my poor wit in loyal service.

sentences.zh: 臣聞金使之來，陛下以祖宗陵寢廢祀，徽宗皇帝、顯肅皇后梓宮在遠，母後春秋已高，久闕晨昏之奉，淵聖皇帝與天族還歸無期，欲屈己以就和，遣使報聘。

translations.literal: I hear that since the Jin envoys came, Your Majesty, because the ancestral tombs lie desolate without sacrifice, the spirit coffins of Emperor Huizong and Empress Xiansu are far away, the Queen Mother is advanced in years and long denied daily attendance, and the Sagely Emperor and the imperial clan have no date for return, wishes to humble yourself to seek peace and has sent envoys to return the visit.
translations.idiomatic: I understand that since the Jin envoys arrived, Your Majesty—because the imperial tombs lie desolate and unhonored, the spirit coffins of Emperor Huizong and Empress Xiansu remain far away, the Queen Mother is advanced in years and long denied your daily attendance, and the Sagely Emperor with the imperial clan have no prospect of return—has been willing to humble yourself to secure peace and has sent envoys to return their visit.

sentences.zh: 茲事體大，固已詔侍從、臺諫各具所見聞矣，不知侍從臺諫皆以為可乎？

translations.literal: This matter is weighty; Your Majesty has already ordered the attendant officials and remonstrators to each submit their views—I do not know whether all the attendants and remonstrators think it acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: This matter is weighty indeed; Your Majesty has already ordered the attendant officials and remonstrators to submit their views separately—do they all consider it acceptable?

sentences.zh: 抑亦可否雜進，而陛下未有所擇乎？

translations.literal: Or is it a mixture of yes and no, and Your Majesty has not yet chosen?
translations.idiomatic: Or have yes and no been offered together, and Your Majesty has not yet chosen among them?

sentences.zh: 抑亦金已恭順，不復邀我以難行之禮乎？

translations.literal: Or have the Jin already become respectful and no longer press impossible ceremonies upon us?
translations.idiomatic: Or have the Jin already become respectful and ceased to demand ceremonies we cannot possibly perform?

sentences.zh: 是數者，臣所不得而聞也。

translations.literal: Of these several points, your servant cannot hear and does not know.
translations.idiomatic: On these several points your servant has not been able to learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 請試別白利害，為陛下詳陳之。

translations.literal: Allow me to sort profit and harm separately and lay them out in detail for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Permit me to sort benefit and harm separately and set them out in detail for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 夫金人始入寇也，固嘗雲講和矣。

translations.literal: When the Jin first invaded, they indeed claimed they would negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin first invaded, they repeatedly claimed they wished to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 靖康之初，約肅王至大河而返，已而挾之北行，訖無音耗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang they agreed that Prince Su would reach the Yellow River and return, then seized him and marched north, and thereafter there was no word.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingkang crisis they agreed that Prince Su would reach the Yellow River and return; instead they seized him and marched north, and thereafter no word came.

sentences.zh: 河朔千里，焚掠無遺，老稚系累而死者億萬計，復破威勝、隆德等州。

translations.literal: For a thousand li north of the river they burned and plundered without leaving anything; old and young bound in strings died by the tens and millions; they also took Weisheng and Longde prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand li north of the river they burned and plundered without sparing anything; the old and young, bound in chains, died by the tens of millions; they also overran Weisheng, Longde, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 淵聖皇帝嘗降詔書，謂金人渝盟，必不可守。

translations.literal: The Sagely Emperor once issued an edict saying the Jin had violated the alliance and it absolutely must not be kept.
translations.idiomatic: The Sagely Emperor once issued an edict declaring that the Jin had violated the alliance and that it absolutely must not be honored.

sentences.zh: 是歲又復深入，朝廷制置失宜，都城遂陷。

translations.literal: That year they invaded again; the court's arrangements were wrong and the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: That same year they invaded again; the court's dispositions were ill judged, and the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 敵情狡甚，懼我百萬之眾必以死爭也，止我諸道勤王之師，則又曰講和矣。

translations.literal: The enemy were exceedingly cunning; fearing our million troops would fight to the death, they halted our relief armies from all circuits—then again said they would negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy were exceedingly cunning; fearing that our million troops would fight to the death, they halted the relief armies marching from every circuit—then again spoke of negotiating peace.

sentences.zh: 乃邀淵聖出郊，次邀徽宗繼往，追取宗族，殆無虛日，傾竭府庫，靡有孑遺，公卿大臣類皆拘執，然後偽立張邦昌而去。

translations.literal: They invited the Sagely Emperor out beyond the walls, then invited Huizong in turn, continually seized members of the clan almost without a vacant day, drained the treasuries leaving not a scrap, detained the great ministers—then falsely enthroned Zhang Bangchang and left.
translations.idiomatic: They lured the Sagely Emperor beyond the walls, then summoned Huizong in turn; day after day they seized members of the imperial clan, drained the treasuries until nothing remained, detained the great ministers—and only then falsely enthroned Zhang Bangchang and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 則是金人所謂“講和”者，果可信乎？

translations.literal: So the Jin's so-called "negotiate peace"—can it truly be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: Can the Jin's so-called "peace negotiations" truly be trusted?

sentences.zh: 此已然之禍，陛下所親見。

translations.literal: This is calamity Your Majesty has seen with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: This is calamity Your Majesty has witnessed with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 今徒以王倫繆悠之說，遂誘致金人責我以必不可行之禮，而陛下遂已屈己從之，臣是以不覺涕泗之橫流也。

translations.literal: Now on Wang Lun's reckless talk alone, the Jin are induced to demand ceremonies we absolutely cannot perform—and Your Majesty has already humbled yourself to comply; your servant cannot help weeping floods of tears.
translations.idiomatic: Now on Wang Lun's reckless talk alone the Jin have been induced to demand ceremonies we absolutely cannot perform—and Your Majesty has already humbled yourself to comply; your servant cannot keep tears from streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 而彼以“詔諭江南”為名而來，則是飛尺書而下本朝，豈講和之謂哉？

translations.literal: Yet they come in the name of "Edict instructing Jiangnan"—sending a one-foot document to command our dynasty; how is this called negotiating peace?
translations.idiomatic: Yet they come under the title "Imperial Edict Instructing Jiangnan"—flinging down a brief document to command our dynasty; how can this be called negotiating peace?

sentences.zh: 我躬受之，真為臣妾矣。

translations.literal: We receive it in person—we truly become their subjects.
translations.idiomatic: We receive it in person—we truly become their subjects and servants.

sentences.zh: 陛下方寢苫枕塊，其忍下穹廬之拜乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just lying on the mourning mat—how can you bear to bow beneath their felt tents?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty still lies upon the mourning mat—how can you bear to bow beneath their felt tents?

sentences.zh: 臣竊料陛下必不忍為也。

translations.literal: Your servant privately judges Your Majesty surely cannot bring yourself to do it.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant privately judges that Your Majesty surely cannot bring yourself to do it.

sentences.zh: 萬一奉其詔令，則將變置吾之大臣，分部吾之諸將，邀求無厭，靡有窮極。

translations.literal: If by any chance you accept their edict, they will then reshuffle our great ministers, divide control of our generals, and their demands will know no end.
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance you accept their edict, they will reshuffle our great ministers, divide authority over our generals, and their demands will know no end.

sentences.zh: 當此之時，陛下欲從之則無以立國，不從之則復責我以違令，其何以自處乎？

translations.literal: At that time if Your Majesty wishes to comply you cannot preserve the state; if you refuse they will again blame us for disobeying—how will you situate yourself?
translations.idiomatic: At that point, if Your Majesty complies you cannot preserve the state; if you refuse they will blame us for defying their command—how will Your Majesty then position yourself?

sentences.zh: 況犬羊之群，驚動我陵寢，戕毀我宗廟，劫遷我二帝，據守我祖宗之地，塗炭我祖宗之民，而又徽宗皇帝、顯肅皇后鑒輿不返，遂致萬國痛心，是謂不共戴天之仇。

translations.literal: Moreover these wolf-and-goat packs have disturbed our imperial tombs, destroyed our ancestral temples, seized our two emperors, hold our ancestral lands, torment our ancestral people—and Huizong and Xiansu's palanquins never return, making the ten thousand states ache with grief: this is a feud we cannot share the sky with.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover these wolf-and-goat hordes have disturbed our imperial tombs, destroyed our ancestral temples, carried off our two emperors, hold our ancestral lands, and torment our people—while the palanquins of Emperor Huizong and Empress Xiansu have never returned, stirring grief throughout the realm: this is a feud for which we cannot share the same sky.

sentences.zh: 彼意我之必復此仇也，未嘗頃刻而忘圖我，豈一王倫能平哉？

translations.literal: They believe we must surely seek this revenge and have never for a moment ceased plotting against us—can one Wang Lun smooth it over?
translations.idiomatic: They believe we must surely seek this revenge and have never for a moment ceased plotting against us—can one Wang Lun smooth it over?

sentences.zh: 方王倫之為此行也，雖閭巷之人，亦知其取笑外夷，為國生事。

translations.literal: When Wang Lun undertook this mission, even lane and alley folk knew he invited ridicule from foreigners and created trouble for the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lun undertook this mission, even men in the lanes and alleys knew he invited ridicule from foreigners and created trouble for the state.

sentences.zh: 今無故誘狂敵悖慢如此，若猶倚信其說而不寢，誠可慟哭，使賈誼復生，謂國有人乎哉，無人乎哉？

translations.literal: Now without cause the mad enemy insults us so; if we still trust their talk and do not stop, it is truly a cause for wailing—if Jia Yi were reborn would he say the state has men or has no men?
translations.idiomatic: Now, without cause, the enemy insult us so brazenly; if we still trust their words and do not desist, it is truly a cause for wailing—if Jia Yi were reborn, would he say the state still has men, or that it has none?

sentences.zh: 古之外夷，固有不得已而事之以皮幣、事之以珠玉、事之以犬馬者，曷嘗有受其詔，惟外夷之欲是從，如今日事哉！

translations.literal: Barbarians of old—when they had to submit, some offered furs and silks, pearls and jade, dogs and horses—when was there accepting their edicts, obeying whatever barbarians wished, as today?
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians of old, when compelled to submit, might offer furs and silks, pearls and jade, dogs and horses—but when did they accept edicts and obey whatever barbarians desired, as we face today?

sentences.zh: 脫或包羞忍恥，受其詔諭，而彼所以許我者不復如約，則徒受莫大之辱，貽萬世之譏；

translations.literal: If we swallow shame and accept their edict, and what they promise fails as agreed, we suffer boundless disgrace and leave eternal ridicule;
translations.idiomatic: If we swallow shame and accept their edict, and what they promise us fails to match their word, we suffer boundless disgrace and leave eternal ridicule;

sentences.zh: 縱使如約，則是我今日所有土地，先拱手而奉外夷矣，祖宗在天之靈，以謂如何？

translations.literal: Even if they keep their word, all the land we hold today we first offer with bowed hands to foreigners—what would our ancestors' spirits in heaven say?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they keep their word, we would first offer with bowed hands all the land we hold today to foreigners—what would our ancestors' spirits in heaven think?

sentences.zh: 徽宗皇帝、顯肅皇后不共戴天之仇，遂不可復也，豈不能痛哉！

translations.literal: The feud of Huizong and Xiansu could never be avenged—can we not grieve?
translations.idiomatic: The feud against Emperor Huizong and Empress Xiansu could never be avenged—can we not grieve?

sentences.zh: 陛下其審思之，斷非聖心所能安也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should examine this closely—it is surely not what your sage heart can rest upon.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should weigh this carefully—it is surely not what your sage heart can rest upon.

sentences.zh: 自金使入境以來，內外惶惑，儻或陛下終以王倫之說為不妄，金人之詔為可從，臣恐不惟墮外夷之奸計，而意外之虞，將有不可勝言者矣。

translations.literal: Since the Jin envoys entered, inside and outside are in alarm; if Your Majesty finally holds Wang Lun's words not false and the Jin edict acceptable, your servant fears not only falling into the barbarians' plot but disasters beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin envoys entered the realm, court and country alike have been in alarm; if Your Majesty finally judges Wang Lun's words sound and the Jin edict acceptable, your servant fears we will not only fall into the barbarians' plot but face calamities beyond words.

sentences.zh: 此眾所共曉，陛下亦嘗慮及於此乎？

translations.literal: This everyone understands—has Your Majesty also considered it?
translations.idiomatic: This everyone understands—has Your Majesty also considered it?

sentences.zh: 國家兩嘗敗外夷於淮甸，雖未能克復中原之地，而大江之南亦足支吾。

translations.literal: The state twice defeated foreigners on the Huai, and though we could not recover the Central Plain, south of the Great River we can still sustain ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: The state has twice defeated the barbarians on the Huai; though we have not recovered the Central Plain, the lands south of the Great River are still sufficient to sustain us.

sentences.zh: 軍聲粗震，國勢粗定，故金人因王倫之往復，遣使來嘗試朝廷。

translations.literal: Military renown has somewhat revived, the state's position somewhat stabilized—so the Jin because of Wang Lun's going and coming sent envoys to test the court.
translations.idiomatic: Our military renown has somewhat revived and the state's position somewhat stabilized; the Jin, because of Wang Lun's shuttling back and forth, have sent envoys to probe the court.

sentences.zh: 我若從其所請，正墮計中；

translations.literal: If we grant their request we fall exactly into their scheme;
translations.idiomatic: If we grant their request we fall exactly into their scheme;

sentences.zh: 不從其欲，且厚攜我之金幣而去，亦何適而非彼之利哉！

translations.literal: if we refuse, they still carry away our gold and silk in abundance—is any course not to their advantage?
translations.idiomatic: if we refuse, they still depart laden with our gold and silk—in what way is any course not to their advantage?

sentences.zh: 為今之計，獨有陛下幡然改慮，布告中外，以收人心，謂祖宗陵寢廢祀，徽宗皇帝、顯肅皇后梓宮在遠，母後、淵聖、宗枝族屬未還，故遣使迎請，冀遂南歸。

translations.literal: For today's plan, only if Your Majesty suddenly changes your deliberations, proclaims inside and outside to recover hearts, saying that because ancestral tombs lie desolate, Huizong and Xiansu's coffins are far, the Queen Mother, Sagely Emperor, and imperial kin not returned, envoys were sent to welcome them home.
translations.idiomatic: For today's plan, Your Majesty alone must suddenly change course, proclaim throughout the realm to recover popular hearts, and explain that because the imperial tombs lie desolate, the coffins of Emperor Huizong and Empress Xiansu remain far away, and the Queen Mother, the Sagely Emperor, and the imperial clansmen have not returned, envoys were sent to welcome them south.

sentences.zh: 今敵之來，邀朝廷以必不可從之禮，實王倫賣國之罪，當行誅責，以釋天下之疑。

translations.literal: Now the enemy come demanding ceremonies the court absolutely cannot perform—this is Wang Lun's crime of selling the state and he should be punished to release the world's doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Now the enemy come demanding ceremonies the court absolutely cannot perform—this is Wang Lun's crime of betraying the state; he should be punished to dispel the world's doubts.

sentences.zh: 然後激厲諸將，謹捍邊陲，無墮敵計，進用忠正，黜遠奸邪，以振紀綱，以修政事，務為實效，不事虛名，夕慮朝謀，以圖興復，庶乎可矣。

translations.literal: Then stir the generals, guard the borders carefully, do not fall into enemy schemes, promote the loyal, remove the treacherous far off, rectify discipline, repair government, seek real results not empty names, plan morning and evening for restoration—then perhaps it can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Then rouse the generals, guard the frontiers diligently, do not fall into enemy schemes, promote the loyal and upright and banish the treacherous far away, restore discipline, repair government, seek real results rather than empty reputation, and plan morning and evening for restoration—then perhaps success is possible.

sentences.zh: 今金使雖已就館，謂當別議區處之宜。

translations.literal: Though the Jin envoy is already lodged, it is fitting to discuss separately how to handle him.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Jin envoy is already lodged in the guest residence, it is fitting to discuss separately how he should be handled.

sentences.zh: 臣聞萬人所聚，必有公言。

translations.literal: I hear wherever ten thousand gather there must be public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that wherever ten thousand gather, public opinion must emerge.

sentences.zh: 今在廷百執事之臣，與中外一心，皆以金人之詔為不可從，公言如此，陛下獨不察乎？

translations.literal: Now every official at court and all within and without are of one mind that the Jin edict cannot be obeyed—such is the public voice; does Your Majesty alone not perceive it?
translations.idiomatic: Now every official at court, and the realm within and without, are of one mind that the Jin edict cannot be obeyed—such is the public voice; does Your Majesty alone not perceive it?

sentences.zh: 若夫謂粘罕之已死，外夷內亂，契丹林牙復立，故今金主復與我平等語，是皆行詐款我師之計，非臣所敢知也。

translations.literal: As for saying Nianhan is dead, barbarians are in internal disorder, the Liao Linya has been restored, so the Jin ruler again treats us as equals—all are schemes of false reassurance to deceive our army, not what your servant dares know.
translations.idiomatic: As for claims that Nianhan is dead, the barbarians are torn by internal disorder, and the Khitan Linya has been restored, so that the Jin ruler again speaks to us as an equal—all are schemes of false reassurance to deceive our forces, matters your servant cannot presume to judge.

sentences.zh: 或者又謂金使在館，今稍恭順。

translations.literal: Or some say the Jin envoy at the lodge is now somewhat respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Some also say the Jin envoy at the guest residence has lately become somewhat respectful.

sentences.zh: 如臣之所聞，又何其悖慢於前，而遽設恭順於後？

translations.literal: From what your servant hears, how is he more arrogant than before yet suddenly respectful after?
translations.idiomatic: From what your servant has heard, how can he have been so insolent before and suddenly put on respect afterward?

sentences.zh: 敵情變詐百出，豈宜惟聽其甘言，遂忘備預之深計，待其禍亂之已至，又無所及？

translations.literal: Enemy temperament shifts in a hundred deceits—should we only heed sweet words, forget deep precaution, and when calamity comes have no remedy?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy shift their schemes in a hundred ways—should we heed only their sweet words, forget our deepest precautions, and find ourselves helpless when calamity arrives?

sentences.zh: 此誠切於事情。

translations.literal: This truly bears on the matter at hand.
translations.idiomatic: This truly bears directly on the matter at hand.

sentences.zh: 今日之舉，存亡所系，愚衷感發，不能自己，望鑒其惓惓之忠，特垂采納，更與三二大臣熟議其便，無貽異時之悔，社稷天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Today's act bears on survival itself; naive loyalty overflows—I beg you discern this earnest loyalty, specially adopt it, discuss further with two or three great ministers, lest regret come in another day; the altars and realm would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: Today's decision bears on the survival of the state; my earnest loyalty overflows and I cannot restrain myself. I beg Your Majesty to discern this devoted loyalty, adopt it in special measure, and discuss it thoroughly with two or three senior ministers, lest regret come in another day. The altars of state and the realm would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 疏入，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no response.

sentences.zh: 後忻托故乞從外補，乃授荊湖南路轉運判官。

translations.literal: Later Xin pleaded illness as a pretext to seek an external appointment, and was then made Transport Vice Commissioner for Jinghu Nan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xu Xin pleaded illness as a pretext to seek an appointment outside the capital and was made Transport Vice Commissioner for Jinghu Nan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 謫居撫州，起知邵陽，卒。

translations.literal: Exiled to dwell in Fuzhou, later summoned to know Shaoyang, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Exiled to Fuzhou, he was later recalled to serve as prefect of Shaoyang and died there.

sentences.zh: 應孟明，字仲實，婺州永康人。

translations.literal: Ying Mengming, styled Zhongshi, was a man of Yongkang in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Mengming, styled Zhongshi, was a native of Yongkang in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 少入太學，登隆興元年進士第。

translations.literal: In youth he entered the Imperial Academy and passed the jinshi in the first year of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he entered the Imperial Academy and passed the jinshi examination in the first year of the Longxing reign.

sentences.zh: 試中教官，調臨安府教授，繼為浙東安撫司幹官、樂平縣丞。

translations.literal: He passed the instructor examination, was assigned professor of Lin'an prefecture, then served as staff officer of the Zhedong Pacification Commission and assistant magistrate of Leping County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the instructor examination, was appointed professor at the Lin'an prefectural school, and later served as administrative officer on the Zhedong Pacification Commission and as assistant magistrate of Leping County.

sentences.zh: 侍御史葛邲、監察御史王藺薦為詳定一司敕令所刪定官。

translations.literal: Supervising Attendant Censor Ge Min and Investigating Censor Wang Lan recommended him as reviser at the Commission for Revising Statutes of a Single Department.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretariat Attendant Ge Min and Investigating Censor Wang Lan recommended him as a reviser at the Commission for Revising and Compiling Statutes of a Single Department.

sentences.zh: 輪對，首論：“南北通好，疆場無虞，當選將練兵，常如大敵之在境，而可以一日忽乎？

translations.literal: At a rotation audience he spoke first: "North and south are on friendly terms and the borders untroubled—yet one should select generals and train troops as though a great enemy were at the frontier; can one neglect this for a single day?
translations.idiomatic: At a rotation audience he spoke first: "North and south enjoy friendly relations and the borders are untroubled—yet should we not select generals and train troops as though a great enemy were at the frontier? Can we neglect this for even a single day?

sentences.zh: 貪殘苛酷之吏未去，吾民得無不安其生者乎？

translations.literal: Greedy, cruel, and harsh officials have not been removed—can our people live without unease for their livelihoods?
translations.idiomatic: Greedy, cruel, and oppressive officials have not been removed—can our people live in security?

sentences.zh: 賢士匿於下僚，忠言壅於上聞，無乃眾正之門未盡開，而兼聽之意未盡孚乎？

translations.literal: Worthy men hide among junior posts and loyal words are blocked from reaching above—is it not that the gates for the many upright have not been fully opened, and the intent to hear all sides not fully fulfilled?
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men hide among junior posts and loyal counsel is blocked from reaching the throne—is it not that the gates for the upright have not been fully opened, and the spirit of hearing all sides not fully honored?

sentences.zh: 君臣之間，戒懼而不自持，勤勞而不自寧，進君子，退小人，以民隱為憂，以邊陲為警，則政治自修，紀綱自張矣。”

translations.literal: Between ruler and minister, being vigilant without indulging ease, laboring without resting in comfort, advancing gentlemen and removing petty men, taking the people's hidden suffering as concern and the frontier as warning—then government will right itself and discipline extend itself."
translations.idiomatic: Between ruler and minister, if both remain vigilant without indulging ease, labor without resting in comfort, advance gentlemen and remove petty men, take the people's hidden suffering as their concern and the frontier as their warning—then government will right itself and discipline will extend of its own accord."

sentences.zh: 孝宗曰：“朕早夜戒懼，無頃刻忘，退朝之暇，亦無它好，正恐臨朝或稍晏，則萬幾之曠自此始矣。”

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong said: "I am vigilant day and night without a moment's forgetfulness; in leisure after court I have no other diversion—only fearing that if attending court is slightly late, the neglect of myriad affairs begins from there."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong said: "I am vigilant day and night without a moment's forgetfulness; in the leisure after court I have no other diversion—only fearing that if I attend court even slightly late, the neglect of myriad affairs begins from that moment."

sentences.zh: 次乞申嚴監司庇貪吏之禁，薦舉徇私情之禁，帝嘉獎久之。

translations.literal: Next he requested strict enforcement of prohibitions against supervisory officials sheltering greedy clerks and against nepotism in recommendations; the Emperor praised him at length.
translations.idiomatic: He next asked that prohibitions be strictly enforced against supervisory officials who shield corrupt clerks and against favoritism in recommendations; the Emperor praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 它日，宰相進擬，帝出片紙於掌中，書二人姓名，曰：“卿何故不及此？”

translations.literal: Another day, when the chief ministers presented nominations, the Emperor produced a slip of paper from his palm with two names written on it, saying: "Why did you not reach this far?"
translations.idiomatic: On another day, when the chief ministers presented nominations, the Emperor produced a slip of paper from his palm with two names written on it and said: "Why did you not include these men?"

sentences.zh: 其一則孟明也。

translations.literal: One was Mengming.
translations.idiomatic: One of them was Mengming.

sentences.zh: 乃拜大理寺丞。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 故大將李顯忠之子家僮溺死，有司誣以殺人，逮系幾三百家。

translations.literal: A household servant of the son of the former great general Li Xianzhong had drowned; the authorities falsely charged murder, and nearly three hundred households were arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: A household servant of the son of the former great general Li Xianzhong had drowned; the authorities falsely charged murder, and nearly three hundred households were arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 孟明察其冤，白於長官，釋之。

translations.literal: Mengming investigated and found the injustice, reported to his superior, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Mengming investigated the case, found the injustice, reported it to his superior, and had them released.

sentences.zh: 出為福建提舉常平，陛辭，帝曰：“朕知卿愛百姓，惡贓吏，事有不便於民，宜悉意以聞。”

translations.literal: Sent out as Fujian Commissioner for Ever-Normal Granaries; at farewell audience the Emperor said: "I know you love the common people and hate corrupt officials; when anything is inconvenient for the people, you should report it fully."
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Fujian Commissioner for Ever-Normal Granaries. At his farewell audience the Emperor said: "I know you love the common people and hate corrupt officials; when anything is inconvenient for the people, you should report it to me in full."

sentences.zh: 因問當世人才，孟明對曰：“有才而不學，則流為刻薄，惟上之教化明，取舍正，使回心向道，則成就必倍於人。”

translations.literal: He then asked about talent of the age; Mengming replied: "Those with talent but without study become harsh and censorious; only if the ruler's teaching is clear and choices correct, making them turn their hearts to the Way, will achievement surely be twice that of others."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then asked about the talent of the age. Mengming replied: "Those with talent but without learning become harsh and censorious; only if the ruler's teaching is clear and his choices correct, turning their hearts toward the Way, will their achievement surely be twice that of others."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“誠為人上者之責。”

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "That is truly the responsibility of one who stands above others."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "That is truly the responsibility of one who stands above others."

sentences.zh: 孟明至部，具以臨遣之意咨訪之。

translations.literal: When Mengming reached his post he fully consulted according to the intent of his parting audience.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengming reached his post, he thoroughly investigated matters according to the intent of his parting instructions.

sentences.zh: 帝一日禦經筵，因論監司按察，顧謂講讀官曰：“朕近日得數人，應孟明，其最也。”

translations.literal: One day the Emperor attended the classics lecture and, discussing supervisory investigations, turned to the lecture officials and said: "Recently I have obtained several men; Ying Mengming is foremost among them."
translations.idiomatic: One day the Emperor attended the classics lecture and, discussing supervisory investigations, turned to the lecture officials and said: "Recently I have found several capable men; Ying Mengming is foremost among them."

sentences.zh: 尋除浙東提點刑獄，以鄉部引嫌，改使江東。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Zhedong Judicial Commissioner; citing conflict with his native circuit he was reassigned to Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Judicial Commissioner for Zhedong; citing a conflict of interest with his native circuit, he was reassigned to Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 會廣西謀帥，帝謂輔臣曰：“朕熟思之，無易應孟明者。”

translations.literal: When Guangxi sought a commander, the Emperor told his chief ministers: "I have pondered deeply—no one is more suitable than Ying Mengming."
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxi was seeking a commander, the Emperor told his chief ministers: "I have thought this over carefully—no one is more suitable than Ying Mengming."

sentences.zh: 即以手筆賜孟明曰：“朕聞廣西鹽法利害相半，卿到任，自可詳究事實。”

translations.literal: He immediately wrote in his own hand to Mengming: "I have heard the Guangxi salt law is half benefit and half harm; when you take office you may thoroughly investigate the facts."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately wrote to Mengming in his own hand: "I have heard that the Guangxi salt law is half beneficial and half harmful; when you take office you may thoroughly investigate the facts."

sentences.zh: 進直秘閣、知靜江府兼廣西經略安撫。

translations.literal: Promoted to Direct Attendant of the Secretariat, Prefect of Jingjiang and concurrently Guangxi Military Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Secretariat, made prefect of Jingjiang, and concurrently appointed Guangxi Military Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，廣西鹽易官般為客鈔，客戶無多，折閱逃避，遂抑配於民。

translations.literal: Initially Guangxi salt was changed from official transport to merchant certificates; merchants were few, losses and evasion followed, and compulsory allocation upon the people was imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the Guangxi salt trade had been changed from official transport to merchant certificates; merchants were few, losses and evasion followed, and salt was forcibly allocated to the populace.

sentences.zh: 行之六年，公私交病，追逮禁錮，民不聊生。

translations.literal: After six years of implementation, public and private alike were afflicted; pursuit, arrest, and imprisonment—the people could not sustain life.
translations.idiomatic: After six years of this policy, public and private interests alike were ruined; pursuit, arrest, and imprisonment left the people unable to sustain their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 孟明條具驛奏除其弊，詔從之。

translations.literal: Mengming listed the abuses in detail and reported by relay post to abolish them; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Mengming itemized the abuses in a detailed report sent by relay post and petitioned to abolish them; an edict approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 禁卒朱興結集黨侶，弄兵雷、化間，聲勢漸長，孟明遣將縛致轅門斬之。

translations.literal: Garrison soldier Zhu Xing gathered conspirators and raised arms between Lei and Hua; as their power grew, Mengming sent a general to bind him and bring him to the camp gate for execution.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison soldier Zhu Xing gathered a band of conspirators and raised arms between Leizhou and Huazhou; as their power grew, Mengming sent a general to bind him, bring him to the camp gate, and execute him.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，遷浙西提點刑獄，尋召為吏部員外郎，改左司，遷右司，再遷中書門下省檢正諸房公事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, transferred to Zhexi Judicial Commissioner; soon summoned as Vice Director of Personnel, moved to Left Secretariat, then Right Secretariat, again promoted to Rectifier of Affairs for All Bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Judicial Commissioner for Zhexi; he was soon summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, moved to the Left Secretariat, then the Right Secretariat, and was again promoted to Rectifier of Affairs for All Bureaus of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，拜太府卿兼吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong ascended, appointed Minister of the Palace Treasury and concurrently Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong ascended the throne, he was appointed Minister of the Palace Treasury and concurrently Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 慶元初，權吏部侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan, acting Vice Minister of Personnel; he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingyuan reign he served as acting Vice Minister of Personnel and died in office.

sentences.zh: 孟明以儒學奮身受知人主，官職未嘗幸遷。

translations.literal: Mengming rose through Confucian learning and won the sovereign's trust; he never sought advancement by luck.
translations.idiomatic: Mengming rose through Confucian learning and won the sovereign's trust; he never sought advancement by chance or favor.

sentences.zh: 韓侂胄嘗遣其密客誘以諫官，俾誣趙汝愚，孟明不答，士論以此重之。

translations.literal: Han Tuozhou once sent a secret agent to tempt him with the post of remonstrator, making him slander Zhao Ruyu; Mengming did not respond, and scholarly opinion greatly respected him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou once sent a secret agent to tempt him with the post of remonstrator, urging him to slander Zhao Ruyu; Mengming did not respond, and scholarly opinion greatly respected him for this.

sentences.zh: 曾三聘，字無逸，臨江新淦人。

translations.literal: Zeng Sanpin, styled Wuyi, was a man of Xingan in Linjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Sanpin, styled Wuyi, was a native of Xingan in Linjiang.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Qiandao.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Qiandao reign.

sentences.zh: 調贛州司戶參軍，累遷軍器監主簿。

translations.literal: Appointed Recorder of Ganzhou, promoted through ranks to chief clerk of the Directorate of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Recorder of Ganzhou and rose through the ranks to chief clerk of the Directorate of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 有旨造劃車弩，三聘謂：“劃車弩六人挽之，而箭之所及止二百六十步。

translations.literal: An order came to build the sliding-cart crossbow; Sanpin said: "The sliding-cart crossbow requires six men to draw it, yet its range reaches only 260 paces.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order came to build the sliding-cart crossbow. Sanpin said: "The sliding-cart crossbow requires six men to draw it, yet its range reaches only two hundred and sixty paces.

sentences.zh: 今所用克敵弓較之，工費不及十之三，一人挽之而射可及三百六十步，利害曉然。”

translations.literal: Compared with the Ke-di bow now in use, the labor and cost are less than three-tenths; one man can draw it and shoot 360 paces—the advantage and harm are obvious."
translations.idiomatic: Compared with the enemy-defeating bow now in use, the labor and cost amount to less than three-tenths; one man can draw it and shoot three hundred and sixty paces—the advantage and disadvantage are obvious."

sentences.zh: 乃不果造。

translations.literal: The project was therefore not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The project was therefore not carried out.

sentences.zh: 光宗不朝重華宮，中外疑懼，三聘以書抵丞相留正。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangzong did not attend Chonghua Palace; court and country were anxious; Sanpin wrote to Chief Councilor Liu Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangzong ceased attending Chonghua Palace; court and country were filled with anxiety, and Sanpin wrote to Chief Councilor Liu Zheng.

sentences.zh: 正未及言，會以它事不合求去。

translations.literal: Before Zheng could speak, he happened to disagree over another matter and requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: Before Liu Zheng could speak, he happened to disagree with the Emperor over another matter and requested leave.

sentences.zh: 三聘謂：“丞相今泯默而退耶，亦將取今日所難言者別白言之而後退？

translations.literal: Sanpin said: "Will the Chief Councilor now retire in silence, or will you take what is hard to say today and set it forth clearly before retiring?
translations.idiomatic: Sanpin said: "Will the Chief Councilor now retire in silence, or will you take what is hard to say today and set it forth clearly before you withdraw?

sentences.zh: 凡今闕庭之內，閨門衽席之間，父子夫婦之際，群臣莫敢深言者，避嫌遠罪耳。

translations.literal: All within the palace halls now, between bed curtains in the inner quarters, at the juncture of father-son and husband-wife—what no minister dares speak of deeply is only avoiding suspicion and fleeing blame.
translations.idiomatic: All that occurs within the palace halls, between the bed curtains of the inner quarters, at the juncture of father and son and husband and wife—what no minister dares speak of deeply is only to avoid suspicion and flee blame.

sentences.zh: 丞相身退計決，言之何嫌乎？”

translations.literal: The Chief Councilor's plan to retire is decided—what suspicion is there in speaking?"
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Councilor's plan to retire is already decided—what suspicion is there in speaking out?"

sentences.zh: 遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 帝欲幸玉津園，三聘上疏言：“今人心既離，大亂將作，小大之臣震怖請命，而陛下安意肆誌而弗聞知，萬一敵人諜知，馳一介之使，問安北宮，不知何以答之？

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to visit Yujin Garden; Sanpin submitted a memorial: "Now hearts are already alienated, great disorder is about to break out, ministers great and small tremble in terror begging for orders—yet Your Majesty indulges your will and gives no heed; if by chance the enemy's spies learn and send a single envoy to inquire after the Northern Palace, how will you answer?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to visit Yujin Garden. Sanpin submitted a memorial: "Hearts are already alienated and great disorder is about to break out; ministers great and small tremble in terror begging for orders—yet Your Majesty indulges your will and gives no heed. If by chance the enemy's spies learn of this and send a single envoy to inquire after the Northern Palace, how will you answer?

sentences.zh: 奸宄窺間，傳一紙之檄，指斥乘輿，不知何以禦之？

translations.literal: Villains watch for openings; pass a single proclamation denouncing the imperial carriage—how will you resist?
translations.idiomatic: If villains watch for an opening and circulate a single proclamation denouncing the imperial carriage, how will you resist it?

sentences.zh: 望亟備法駕朝謁，不然，臣實未知死所也。”

translations.literal: I beg you urgently to prepare the imperial retinue for an audience; otherwise your servant truly does not know where to die.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you urgently to prepare the imperial retinue for an audience at once; otherwise your servant truly does not know where he may die."

sentences.zh: 孝宗病革，復上疏言：“道路流言，洶洶日甚，臣恐不幸而有狂夫奸人，托忠憤以行詐，假曲直以動眾，至此而後悔之，則恐無及矣。”

translations.literal: When Xiaozong was critically ill he again submitted a memorial: "Rumors on the roads grow more tumultuous daily; your servant fears lest by misfortune reckless men and villains, feigning loyal indignation to practice deceit, borrow right and wrong to move the masses—to regret only then will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong was critically ill, he again submitted a memorial: "Rumors on the roads grow more tumultuous by the day; your servant fears that, by misfortune, reckless men and villains may feign loyal indignation to practice deceit and borrow disputes over right and wrong to stir the masses—to regret only then will be too late."

sentences.zh: 帝意為動。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was moved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was moved by this.

sentences.zh: 及孝宗崩，帝疾不能執喪，朝論益震洶，三聘謂今日事勢，莫若建儲。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong died, the Emperor was ill and unable to perform mourning; court discussion grew ever more turbulent; Sanpin said that given the situation today, nothing was better than establishing an heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong died, the Emperor was ill and unable to perform mourning; court discussion grew ever more turbulent. Sanpin said that given the situation today, nothing was more urgent than establishing an heir.

sentences.zh: 或戒之曰：“前日臺諫諸公謂汝奪其職，今復有疏耶？”

translations.literal: Someone warned him: "The other day the remonstrators said you were stealing their duty—will you submit another memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned him: "The other day the remonstrators said you were stealing their duty—will you submit another memorial now?"

sentences.zh: 三聘曰：“此何時而可避煩言也。”

translations.literal: Sanpin said: "At a time like this how can one avoid troublesome words?"
translations.idiomatic: Sanpin said: "At a time like this, how can one avoid speaking what must be said?"

sentences.zh: 寧宗立，兼考功郎，後知郢州。

translations.literal: When Ningzong was established, concurrently Review of Merit; later prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ningzong was established, he served concurrently as Reviewer of Merit and was later appointed prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 會韓侂胄為相，指三聘為故相趙汝愚腹心，坐追兩官。

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou became chief minister, he identified Sanpin as a confidant of the former chief minister Zhao Ruyu and on that account stripped two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Tuozhou became chief minister, he identified Sanpin as a confidant of the former chief minister Zhao Ruyu and on that account stripped him of two ranks.

sentences.zh: 久之，復元官與祠。

translations.literal: After a long while, his original office and temple sinecure were restored.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, his original office and temple sinecure were restored.

sentences.zh: 差知郴州，改提點廣西、湖北刑獄，皆辭不赴。

translations.literal: Assigned prefect of Chenzhou, changed to Judicial Commissioner for Guangxi and Hubei—all declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as prefect of Chenzhou and then transferred to Judicial Commissioner for Guangxi and Hubei; he declined all appointments.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，諸賢遭竄斥者相繼召用，三聘祿不及，終不自言。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was executed, worthy men who had suffered exile were summoned in succession; Sanpin's salary did not reach him, and to the end he never spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou was executed, worthy men who had suffered exile were summoned in succession, but Sanpin's salary never reached him, and to the end he never spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙間，三聘已卒，有旨特贈三官，直龍圖閣，賜謚忠節。

translations.literal: During the Jiading era Sanpin had already died; an order specially posthumously promoted three ranks, made Direct Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and bestowed the posthumous name Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiading era Sanpin had already died; an edict specially posthumously promoted him three ranks, made him Direct Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, and bestowed the posthumous name Zhongjie (Loyal Integrity).

sentences.zh: 徐僑，字崇甫，婺州義烏人。

translations.literal: Xu Qiao, styled Chongfu, was a man of Yiwu in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qiao, styled Chongfu, was a native of Yiwu in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 蚤從學於呂祖謙門人葉邽。

translations.literal: Early on he studied under Ye Yi, a disciple of Lü Zuqian.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he studied under Ye Yi, a disciple of Lü Zuqian.

sentences.zh: 淳熙十四年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chunxi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of the Chunxi reign he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調上饒主簿，始登朱熹之門，熹稱其明白剛直，命以“毅”名齋。

translations.literal: Appointed chief clerk of Shangrao; he first entered Zhu Xi's school; Xi praised him as clear, forthright, and firm, and named his study "Yi."
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of Shangrao and first entered Zhu Xi's school. Xi praised him as clear-minded, forthright, and firm, and named his study the Studio of Resolution.

sentences.zh: 入為秘書省正字、校書郎兼吳、益王府教授。

translations.literal: Entered service as Rectifier of Texts in the Secretariat, Collator, and concurrently instructor to the Wu and Yi princes' households.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Rectifier of Texts in the Secretariat, Collator, and concurrently as instructor to the households of the Wu and Yi princes.

sentences.zh: 直寶謨閣、江東提點刑獄，以迕丞相史彌遠劾罷。

translations.literal: Direct Attendant of the Treasure Proclamation Pavilion and Jiangdong Judicial Commissioner; impeached and dismissed for opposing Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Direct Attendant of the Treasure Proclamation Pavilion and Judicial Commissioner for Jiangdong, but was impeached and dismissed for opposing Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan.

sentences.zh: 寶慶初，葛洪、喬行簡代為請祠，迄不受祿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoqing, Ge Hong and Qiao Xingjian repeatedly requested a temple sinecure on his behalf; he never accepted salary to the end.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoqing reign, Ge Hong and Qiao Xingjian repeatedly requested a temple sinecure on his behalf, but he never accepted salary to the end.

sentences.zh: 紹定中，告老，得請。

translations.literal: During Shaoding he requested retirement on grounds of age and was granted it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaoding reign he requested retirement on grounds of age and was granted it.

sentences.zh: 端平初，與諸賢俱被召，遷秘書少監、太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping, together with other worthies he was summoned; promoted Secretary Vice Director and Vice Director of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duanping reign, together with other worthy men he was summoned and promoted to Secretary Vice Director and Vice Director of Rites.

sentences.zh: 趣入覲，手疏數千言，皆感憤剴切，上劘主闕，下逮群臣，分別黑白，無所回隱。

translations.literal: Urged to enter audience, he submitted a handwritten memorial of several thousand words, all indignant and incisive, cutting at the ruler's faults above and reaching to ministers below, distinguishing black from white without turning aside.
translations.idiomatic: Urged to present himself at court, he submitted a handwritten memorial of several thousand words, all indignant and incisive, cutting at the ruler's faults above and reaching down to the ministers below, distinguishing right from wrong without evasion.

sentences.zh: 帝數慰諭之，顧見其衣履垢敝，愀然謂曰：“卿可謂清貧。”

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly comforted him; seeing his clothes and shoes worn and filthy, he said sorrowfully: "You may be called poor in integrity."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor repeatedly comforted him. Seeing his clothes and shoes worn and filthy, he said sorrowfully: "You may truly be called poor in possessions but rich in integrity."

sentences.zh: 僑對曰：“臣不貧，陛下乃貧耳。”

translations.literal: Qiao replied: "Your servant is not poor—Your Majesty is poor."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao replied: "Your servant is not poor—Your Majesty is poor."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“朕何為貧？”

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In what way am I poor?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "In what way am I poor?"

sentences.zh: 僑曰：“陛下國本未建，疆宇日蹙；

translations.literal: Qiao said: "Your Majesty's foundation for the realm is not established, the territory shrinks daily;
translations.idiomatic: Qiao said: "Your Majesty's foundation for the realm is not established and the territory shrinks daily;

sentences.zh: 權幸用事，將帥非材；

translations.literal: favorites wield power, generals lack ability;
translations.idiomatic: favorites wield power and the generals lack ability;

sentences.zh: 旱蝗相仍，盜賊並起；

translations.literal: drought and locusts follow one upon another, bandits rise together;
translations.idiomatic: drought and locusts follow one upon another and bandits rise together;

sentences.zh: 經用無藝，帑藏空虛；

translations.literal: expenditures lack planning, the treasury is empty;
translations.idiomatic: expenditures lack planning and the treasury is empty;

sentences.zh: 民困於橫斂，軍怨於掊克；

translations.literal: the people suffer from exactions, the army resents exploitation;
translations.idiomatic: the people suffer from exactions and the army resents exploitation;

sentences.zh: 群臣養交而天子孤立，國勢阽危而陛下不悟：臣不貧，陛下乃貧耳。”

translations.literal: ministers cultivate factions while the Son of Heaven stands alone, the state's peril hangs by a thread while Your Majesty does not perceive: your servant is not poor, Your Majesty is poor."
translations.idiomatic: ministers cultivate factions while the Son of Heaven stands alone, the state's peril hangs by a thread while Your Majesty does not perceive it: your servant is not poor—Your Majesty is poor."

sentences.zh: 又言：“今女謁、閹宦相為囊橐，誕為二豎，以處國膏肓，而執政大臣又無和、緩之術，陛下此之不慮而耽樂是從，世有扁鵲，將望見而卻走矣。”

translations.literal: He also said: "Now women of influence and eunuchs are purses for each other, playacting as two boys lodged in the nation's marrow—yet the chief ministers lack the art of He and Huan; Your Majesty does not consider this and follows indulgence in pleasure; if there were a Bian Que in the world, he would behold you and turn back in flight."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Now women of influence and eunuchs serve as each other's purses, playacting as the two boys lodged in the nation's marrow—yet the chief ministers lack the healing art of He Que and Huan Yuan. Your Majesty does not consider this and follows indulgence in pleasure. If there were a Bian Que in the world, he would behold you and turn back in flight."

sentences.zh: 時貴妃閻氏方有寵，而內侍董宋臣表裏用事，故僑論及之。

translations.literal: At the time the honored consort Yan was in favor, and the inner attendant Dong Songchen acted in concert inside and out—hence Qiao's discourse touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the honored consort of the Yan clan was in favor, and the inner attendant Dong Songchen wielded power inside and out in concert—hence Qiao's discourse touched on this.

sentences.zh: 帝為之感動改容，咨嗟太息。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved, his expression changed, and he sighed deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was moved; his expression changed and he sighed deeply.

sentences.zh: 明日，手詔罷邊帥之尤無狀者，申儆群臣以朋黨為之戒，命有司裁節中外浮費，而賜僑金帛甚厚。

translations.literal: The next day, by handwritten edict he dismissed the most lawless frontier commanders, warned ministers against faction-making, ordered the authorities to cut extravagant expenses at court and in the provinces, and bestowed on Qiao gold and silk in great quantity.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, by handwritten edict he dismissed the most lawless frontier commanders, warned the ministers against faction-making, ordered the authorities to cut extravagant expenses at court and in the provinces, and bestowed on Qiao gold and silk in great quantity.

sentences.zh: 僑固辭不受。

translations.literal: Qiao firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao firmly declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 侍講，開陳友愛大義，用是復皇子竑爵，請從祀周敦頤、程顥、程頤、張載、朱熹，以趙汝愚侑食寧宗，帝皆如其請。

translations.literal: As attendant lecturer he expounded the great principle of fraternal affection; on this account the prince Gou's title was restored; he requested joint sacrifice to Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi, with Zhao Ruyu accompanying Ningzong in sacrifice—the Emperor granted all as requested.
translations.idiomatic: As attendant lecturer he expounded the great principle of fraternal affection; on this account Prince Gou's title was restored. He requested joint sacrifice to Zhou Dunyi, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi, with Zhao Ruyu accompanying Emperor Ningzong in sacrifice—the Emperor granted all as he requested.

sentences.zh: 金使至，僑以無國書宜館之於外，如叔向辭鄭故事，迕丞相意，力丐休致，帝諭留甚勤。

translations.literal: When Jin envoys arrived, Qiao held that lacking a state letter they should be lodged outside, as in Shuxiang's refusal of Zheng; this offended the chief minister's intent; he earnestly begged retirement; the Emperor urged him to stay with great earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoys arrived, Qiao held that lacking a state letter they should be lodged outside the capital, as in Shuxiang's refusal of Zheng. This offended the chief minister's intent; he earnestly begged to retire, but the Emperor urged him to remain with great earnestness.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎，辭益堅，遂命以內祠侍讀，不得已就職。

translations.literal: Promoted Vice Minister of Works; his refusal grew firmer; he was then appointed attendant reader on temple sinecure; unable to refuse, he took office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works, but his refusal grew firmer; he was then appointed attendant reader on temple sinecure. Unable to refuse further, he took office.

sentences.zh: 遇事盡言。

translations.literal: On affairs of state he spoke without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: On affairs of state he spoke without reserve.

sentences.zh: 以疾申前請，乃以寶謨閣待制奉祠。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he renewed his earlier request; he was then made Attendant Gentleman of the Treasure Proclamation Pavilion on temple sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: On grounds of illness he renewed his earlier request and was then made Attendant Gentleman of the Treasure Proclamation Pavilion on temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚文清。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Wenqing (Cultured Purity).

sentences.zh: 僑嘗言：“比年熹之書滿天下，不過割裂掇拾，以為進取之資，求其專精篤實，能得其所言者蓋鮮。”

translations.literal: Qiao once said: "In recent years Xi's books fill the world, but most only clip and gather scraps as capital for advancement; those who seek dedicated mastery and solid practice who can live up to his words are indeed few."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao once said: "In recent years Xi's books have filled the world, but most people only clip and gather scraps from them as capital for advancement. Those who seek dedicated mastery and solid practice and can live up to what he taught are indeed few."

sentences.zh: 故其學一以真踐實履為尚。

translations.literal: Therefore his learning took sincere practice and real conduct as its sole standard.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore his learning took sincere practice and real conduct as its sole standard.

sentences.zh: 奏對之言，剖析理欲，因致勸懲。

translations.literal: In memorials and audiences he analyzed principle and desire, thereby offering encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorials and audiences he analyzed principle and desire, thereby offering encouragement and warning.

sentences.zh: 弘益為多。

translations.literal: The benefit was great.
translations.idiomatic: The benefit to the realm was great.

sentences.zh: 若其守官居家，清苦刻厲之操，人所難能也。

translations.literal: As to his holding office and dwelling at home, the integrity of austerity and stern discipline was what others could scarcely achieve.
translations.idiomatic: As for his conduct in office and at home, the integrity of austerity and stern self-discipline was what others could scarcely achieve.

sentences.zh: 度正字周卿，合州人。

translations.literal: Du Zheng, styled Zhouqing, was a man of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zheng, styled Zhouqing, was a native of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年進士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi, jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of the Shaoxi reign (1190).

sentences.zh: 歷官為國子監丞。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he became Guozi Supervisor Director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to become Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 時士大夫無賢愚，皆策李全必反而不敢言，正獨上疏極言之，且獻斃全之策有三，其言鯁亮激切。

translations.literal: At the time scholar-officials whether worthy or foolish all plotted that Li Quan would certainly rebel yet dared not speak; Zheng alone memorialized stating it to the utmost, and moreover presented three plans to kill Quan—his words blunt, bright, and sharply impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, whether learned or dull, every scholar-official was privately convinced that Li Quan would rebel, yet none dared say so. Du Zheng alone memorialized forcefully to that effect and offered three strategies for destroying him; his language was blunt, clear, and fiercely urgent.

sentences.zh: 遷軍器少監。

translations.literal: Moved to Vice Director of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言：“陛下推行聖學，當自正家始。”

translations.literal: At audience he said: "Your Majesty in advancing sacred learning ought to begin from rectifying the family."
translations.idiomatic: At a palace audience he said, "Your Majesty, in promoting the sage's learning, should begin with putting your own household in order."

sentences.zh: 進太常少卿。

translations.literal: He advanced to Vice Minister of Rites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 適太廟災，為二說以獻，其一則用朱熹之議，其一則因宋朝廟制而參以熹之議：“自西徂東為一列，每室之後為一室，以藏祧廟之主。

translations.literal: Just then the Imperial Temple burned; he submitted two proposals. One followed Zhu Xi's proposal; one adapted the Song temple system while mixing in Xi's proposal: "From west to east as one row, behind each chamber make a chamber to store the distant-ancestor shrine tablets.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Ancestral Temple caught fire, he offered two designs. The first followed Zhu Xi's recommendations; the second adapted the Song temple layout while incorporating Xi's ideas: "Arrange the halls in a single row from west to east; behind each hall build another hall to house the tablets of distant ancestors.

sentences.zh: 如僖祖廟以次祧主則藏之，昭居左，穆居右，後世穆之祧主藏太祖廟，昭之祧主藏太宗廟。

translations.literal: For example after the Xizu temple, successive distant tablets are stored; Zhao dwells left, Mu dwells right; later generations' Mu distant tablets store in Taizu temple, Zhao distant tablets store in Taizong temple.
translations.idiomatic: For instance, after the temple of Prince Xi, successive distant-ancestor tablets would be stored there; zhao-line ancestors to the left, mu-line to the right. Later mu-line distant tablets would be kept in the temple of Taizu, and zhao-line distant tablets in the temple of Taizong.

sentences.zh: 仁宗為百世不遷之宗，後世昭之祧主則藏之。

translations.literal: Renzong as the hundred-generations unmoved ancestor, later generations' Zhao distant tablets then store there.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong would be the "unmoved for a hundred generations" founder; later zhao-line distant tablets would be stored in his hall.

sentences.zh: 高宗為百世不遷之宗，後世穆之祧主則藏之。

translations.literal: Gaozong as the hundred-generations unmoved ancestor, later generations' Mu distant tablets then store there.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong would hold the same unmoved status; later mu-line distant tablets would be stored there.

sentences.zh: 室之前為兩室；

translations.literal: Before the chambers are two chambers;
translations.idiomatic: In front of each main hall would stand two subsidiary halls;

sentences.zh: 三年祫享，則帷帳幕之通為一室，盡出諸廟主及祧廟主並為一列，合食其上。

translations.literal: At the three-year he sacrifice, then curtain and screen the passages into one chamber, fully bring out all temple lords and distant-shrine lords and make one row, combined feasting above them.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial he sacrifice, curtains would link the halls into one space; all main and distant-ancestor tablets would be brought out in a single row and honored together on the upper altar.
