sentences.zh: 往者此廟為一室，凡遇祫享合祭於室，名為合享，而實未嘗合享。

translations.literal: In the past this temple was one chamber; whenever meeting he sacrifice combined sacrifice in the chamber, named combined feasting, yet in fact had never combined feasting.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly this temple had been treated as a single hall: on he-year rites a so-called "combined sacrifice" was held within one chamber, but it had never truly united all ancestors in one offering.

sentences.zh: 合增此三室，後有藏祧主之所，前有祖宗合食之地，於本朝之制初無更革，而頗已得三年大祫之義。”

translations.literal: Combined increase these three chambers, afterward having a place to store distant lords, beforehand having a place for ancestors combined eating, toward this dynasty's system at first no reform, yet already obtained the three-year great he meaning quite well.
translations.idiomatic: By adding these three halls—storage for distant tablets behind and a true communal altar before—the basic Song system need not be overturned, yet the intent of the great triennial he rite would at last be fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 遷權禮部侍郎兼侍右郎官，兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰。

translations.literal: Moved to Acting Vice Minister of Rites while also Right Department Vice Director, also Associate Editor of National History and Veritable Records Institute Associate Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Acting Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Associate Compiler on the National History and Veritable Records projects.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，轉一官，守禮部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: Moved to Vice Minister of Rites, transferred one rank, held Vice Minister of Rites and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, advanced one grade, and retired while retaining that title.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈四官，賻銀絹三百。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted four ranks, funeral funds silver and silk three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously promoted four ranks, with three hundred strings of silver and silk for funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 所著有《性善堂文集》。

translations.literal: His writings include "Xingshan Tang Collected Works."
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings were entitled Collected Works of the Hall of Innate Goodness.

sentences.zh: 程必，字懷古，徽州休寧人。

translations.literal: Cheng Bi, styled Huaigu, a man of Xiuning, Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Bi, styled Huaigu, was a native of Xiuning in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹熙四年進士。

translations.literal: In Shaoxi year 4, jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of the Shaoxi reign (1193).

sentences.zh: 授昌化主簿，調建康府教授，改知富陽縣，遷主管官告院。

translations.literal: Appointed Changhua Registrar, transferred to Jiankang Prefecture Instructor, changed to magistrate of Fuyang, moved to oversee the Office of Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed registrar of Changhua, then transferred to be instructor at Jiankang Prefecture, later made magistrate of Fuyang County, and then put in charge of the Office of Credentials.

sentences.zh: 歷宗正寺主簿、樞密院編修官，權右司郎官、秘書監丞，江東轉運判官。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Imperial Clan Court, Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, Acting Right Department Director, Secretariat Supervisor, and Transport Commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as director in the Imperial Clan Court, compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, acting director of the Right Secretariat, supervisor of the Secretariat, and transport commissioner for Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，寧宗謂宰臣曰：“程必豈可容其補外？”

translations.literal: At farewell audience, Ningzong told the chief ministers: "How can Cheng Bi be allowed to fill an outside post?"
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave of court, Emperor Ningzong told his chief ministers, "How can we let Cheng Bi go out to a provincial post?"

sentences.zh: 遂復舊職。

translations.literal: He then returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore kept in his former post at the capital.

sentences.zh: 遷浙西提舉常平，又遷秘書丞，升秘書省著作郎，尋為軍器少監兼權左司郎官。

translations.literal: Moved to Western Zhejiang Ever-Normal Granary Intendant, again moved to Secretariat Assistant Director, promoted to Secretariat Compiler, soon made Vice Director of Armaments while Acting Left Department Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries in western Zhejiang, then assistant director of the Secretariat, promoted to compiler in the Secretariat, and soon after made vice director of armaments while acting as director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷國子司業兼國史編修、實錄檢討，兼權直舍人院，遷起居舍人，兼職依舊。

translations.literal: Moved to Guozi Vice Director while also National History Compiler and Veritable Records Reviser, also Acting Duty in the Drafting Academy, moved to Diarist, concurrent posts as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Imperial University while also compiling the national history and revising the veritable records, and concurrently served in the Drafting Academy; he was then made diarist, retaining his other posts.

sentences.zh: 權吏部侍郎，直學士院兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，兼權中書舍人。

translations.literal: Acting Vice Minister of Personnel, Attendant in the Hanlin while also Associate National History and Veritable Records Compiler, also Acting Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of personnel, attendant in the Hanlin Academy while also compiling the national history and veritable records, and concurrently as acting drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎仍兼侍讀，權刑部尚書，封休寧縣男。

translations.literal: Moved to Vice Minister of Rites still also Lecturer-in-Waiting, Acting Minister of Justice, enfeoffed as Baron of Xiuning County.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of rites while continuing as lecturer-in-waiting, acting minister of justice, and enfeoffed as Baron of Xiuning County.

sentences.zh: 授禮部尚書兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰，兼權吏部尚書，拜翰林學士、知制誥，兼修玉牒官，進封子。

translations.literal: Granted Minister of Rites while also Associate National History and Veritable Records Compiler, also Acting Minister of Personnel, invested as Hanlin Academician and Edict Drafter, also Compiler of the Imperial Genealogy, advanced enfeoffment to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of rites while continuing to compile the national history and veritable records, made acting minister of personnel, invested as Hanlin academician and drafter of edicts, put in charge of revising the imperial genealogy, and advanced to the rank of viscount.

sentences.zh: 五上疏丐祠，以煥章閣學士、知建寧府，授福建路招捕使。

translations.literal: Five times memorialized begging a temple sinecure, made Huanzhang Pavilion Academician and prefect of Jianning, granted Fujian Circuit Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After memorializing five times for a temple sinecure, he was made academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion and prefect of Jianning, and appointed pacification commissioner for the Fujian circuit.

sentences.zh: 以舊職提舉玉隆萬壽宮，進封伯。

translations.literal: With his former post as intendant of Yulong Wanshou Palace, advanced enfeoffment to Earl.
translations.idiomatic: He was made intendant of the Yulong Wanshou Palace with his former rank and advanced to earl.

sentences.zh: 進敷文閣學士、知寧國府，改知贛州，皆不赴。

translations.literal: Advanced to Fuwen Pavilion Academician and prefect of Ningguo, changed to prefect of Ganzhou, all not attended.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Fuwen Pavilion and made prefect of Ningguo, then reassigned to Ganzhou, but did not take up either post.

sentences.zh: 進封新安郡侯，加寶文閣學士、知福州兼福建安撫使。

translations.literal: Advanced enfeoffment to Marquis of Xin'an Commandery, added Baowen Pavilion Academician, prefect of Fuzhou while also Fujian Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Marquis of Xin'an Commandery, made academician of the Baowen Pavilion, and appointed prefect of Fuzhou while also serving as pacification commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 再奉祠，又加龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: Again received temple sinecure, again added Longtu Pavilion Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He again received a temple sinecure and was further made academician of the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 以端明殿學士致仕，卒，年七十有九，贈特進、少師。

translations.literal: With Duanming Hall Academician he retired; he died, age seventy-nine, posthumously granted Special Advancement and Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as academician of the Duanming Hall, died at seventy-nine, and was posthumously granted the ranks of Special Advancement and Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 珌十歲詠冰，語出驚人。

translations.literal: Bi at age ten composed on ice; his words came forth startling men.
translations.idiomatic: At ten Cheng Bi wrote a poem on ice whose lines astonished everyone who heard them.

sentences.zh: 直學士院時，寧宗崩，丞相史彌遠夜召必，舉家大驚。

translations.literal: When Attendant in the Academy, Ningzong died; Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan summoned Bi by night—the whole household greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: While he was attendant in the Hanlin Academy, Emperor Ningzong died; Chief Councillor Shi Miyuan summoned him at night, throwing his entire household into alarm.

sentences.zh: 珌妻丞相王淮女也，泣涕，疑有不測，使人間之，知彌遠出迎，而後收涕。

translations.literal: Bi's wife was Chief Councillor Wang Huai's daughter; she wept tears, suspected unforeseen disaster, sent someone to inquire, learned Miyuan had come out to welcome him, and afterward dried her tears.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's wife was the daughter of former Chief Councillor Wang Huai; she wept, fearing some calamity, until a messenger reported that Miyuan had come out to receive him in person—only then did she dry her tears.

sentences.zh: 彌遠與必同入禁中草矯詔，一夕為制誥二十有五。

translations.literal: Miyuan and Bi together entered the forbidden precinct to draft the superseding edict; in one night made twenty-five edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan and Bi entered the palace together to draft the succession edicts, and in a single night produced twenty-five imperial proclamations.

sentences.zh: 初許必政府，楊皇后緘金一囊賜必，必受之不辭，歸視之，其直不貲。

translations.literal: At first he was promised a post in government; Empress Yang sealed gold in one pouch and bestowed it on Bi; Bi received it without declining; returning he looked at it—its value beyond price.
translations.idiomatic: He had initially been promised a place in the government; Empress Yang sent him a sealed pouch of gold, which he accepted without demur. When he opened it at home, its worth was beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 彌遠以是銜之，卒不與共政雲。

translations.literal: Miyuan because of this bore a grudge against him; in the end did not share government with him.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan bore a grudge over this and never let him share power at court.

sentences.zh: 牛大年，字隆叟，揚州人。

translations.literal: Niu Danian, styled Longsou, a man of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Danian, styled Longsou, was a native of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 慶元二年進士。

translations.literal: In Qingyuan year 2, jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Qingyuan reign (1196).

sentences.zh: 歷官將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Through offices he became Director of Works Supervisor Registrar.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become registrar in the Directorate of Imperial Works.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：“人主所當先者，要以天命人心之所系致念焉。

translations.literal: At audience he said: "What the ruler ought to put first is to bring to mind what Heaven's mandate and the people's hearts are tied to.
translations.idiomatic: At a palace audience he said, "What a ruler should consider first is what binds together Heaven's mandate and the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 夫以人主居富貴崇高之位，重而承宗社之托，尊而為臣辟之戴，一指意而眾莫敢違，一動作而人孰敢議，然而天心靡常，則可畏也。”

translations.literal: Now the ruler occupies wealth, nobility, and exalted position, weighty in bearing the charge of altars and state, honored as what ministers and subjects wear on their heads—one intent and none dare disobey, one movement and who dares discuss it; yet Heaven's mind is inconstant, and that is to be feared."
translations.idiomatic: A ruler sits in wealth and eminence, bearing the weight of altars and state, honored as the head upon which all ministers and subjects depend: one gesture and none dare disobey, one act and none dare question it—yet Heaven's favor is inconstant, and that is what should inspire awe."

sentences.zh: 又言：“今日士氣亦久靡矣，宜體立國之意以振起之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Today scholar spirit has long been dissipated; one ought to embody the intent of founding the state to rouse it.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Scholar-official morale has long been enervated; Your Majesty should take to heart the spirit in which the dynasty was founded and revive it.

sentences.zh: 夫有扶持作興之意，而後縉紳無貪名嗜利之習；

translations.literal: Only with intent to support and raise them will girdled sashes afterward lack the habit of coveting fame and craving profit;
translations.idiomatic: Only when the throne shows a will to support and uplift them will the gentry cease their habit of chasing fame and profit;

sentences.zh: 無貪名嗜利之習，而後有持正秉義之操。

translations.literal: without the habit of coveting fame and craving profit, afterward there will be the conduct of holding to rectitude and grasping righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: and only then will they uphold rectitude and hold fast to principle.

sentences.zh: 國家之休戚，在士大夫之風俗，而風俗之善惡在朝廷。

translations.literal: The state's weal and woe lie in scholar-official custom, and custom's good and evil lie in the court.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty's fortune rests on the manners of its scholar-officials, and those manners depend on the court.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下為之振起，機括一運，天下轉移，而風俗易矣。”

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty rouse it; the mechanism turns once, all under Heaven shifts, and custom changes.
translations.idiomatic: Only Your Majesty can rouse them: turn the lever once, and the realm will shift—custom will change with it."

sentences.zh: 遷軍器監主簿、大宗正丞、四川提舉茶馬兼權總領、知黎州兼管內安撫司公事、節制黎雅州屯戍軍馬，加直寶章閣，為工部郎官。

translations.literal: Moved to Armaments Supervisor Registrar, Imperial Clan Vice Director, Sichuan Tea-Horse Intendant while Acting Overall Controller, prefect of Lizhou while also Inner Pacification Office duties, controlling garrisoned troops of Li and Ya prefectures, added Direct Baozhang Pavilion, made Works Department Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to registrar in the Directorate of Armaments, vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, and intendant of tea and horses in Sichuan while acting as overall controller; made prefect of Lizhou with duties in the inner pacification office and command over garrison troops in Li and Ya prefectures; granted direct access to the Baozhang Pavilion; and appointed director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 入對，請懲貪吏。

translations.literal: At audience, requested punishment of corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: At a palace audience he asked that corrupt officials be punished.

sentences.zh: 遷侍左郎中，進直華文閣、浙東提點刑獄，遷守秘書少監、宗正少卿，升秘書監，遷起居舍人，升起居郎兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Moved to Left Attendant Service Director, advanced to Direct Huawen Pavilion and Eastern Zhejiang Judicial Intendant, moved to hold Secretariat Vice Director and Imperial Clan Vice Director, promoted to Secretariat Director, moved to Diarist, promoted to Senior Diarist while also Chongzheng Hall Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director in the Left Service, granted direct access to the Huawen Pavilion and appointed judicial intendant for eastern Zhejiang, then made acting vice director of the Secretariat and vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, promoted to director of the Secretariat, made diarist, and then senior diarist while also lecturing in the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 以寶章閣待制提舉太平興國宮，卒，特贈四官。

translations.literal: With Baozhang Pavilion Awaiting Orders as intendant of Taiping Xingguo Palace, he died; specially posthumously granted four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: As a Baozhang Pavilion awaiting-orders academician he was made intendant of the Taiping Xingguo Palace; he died and was specially posthumously promoted four ranks.

sentences.zh: 大年清操凜然，所至以廉潔自將。

translations.literal: Danian's pure conduct was stern and awe-inspiring; wherever he went he took integrity and frugality as his guide.
translations.idiomatic: Danian's integrity was austere and commanding; everywhere he served he held himself to scrupulous honesty.

sentences.zh: 陳仲微，字致廣，瑞州高安人。

translations.literal: Chen Zhongwei, styled Zhiguang, a man of Gao'an, Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhongwei, styled Zhiguang, was a native of Gao'an in Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 其先居江州，旌表義門。

translations.literal: His ancestors dwelt in Jiangzhou; a righteous household gate was marked with commendation.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long lived in Jiangzhou, where the gate of their communal household was honored as a model of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 嘉泰二年，舉進士。

translations.literal: In Jiatai year 2, raised as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Jiatai reign (1202).

sentences.zh: 調莆田尉，會守令闕，通判又疲軟不任，臺閫委以縣事。

translations.literal: Transferred to Putian Assistant Magistrate; it happened the prefect and magistrate posts were vacant, the vice prefect was also lax and incompetent, and the surveillance circuit entrusted him with county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as assistant magistrate of Putian; when both the prefect and county magistrate were absent and the vice prefect proved too weak to govern, the surveillance commission put him in charge of county affairs.

sentences.zh: 時歲兇，部卒並饑民作亂，仲微立召首亂者戮之。

translations.literal: At the time the year was famine; garrison soldiers together with starving people made disorder; Zhongwei immediately summoned the chief rioters and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Famine had struck; garrison troops and starving civilians rose in disorder. Zhongwei at once had the ringleaders seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 籍閉糶，抑強糴一境以肅。

translations.literal: He registered and closed government grain sales, suppressed powerful forced purchases throughout the district to bring order.
translations.idiomatic: He registered households, shut down illicit grain sales, and curbed powerful families' forced purchases until the whole district was pacified.

sentences.zh: 囊山浮屠與郡學爭水利，久不決，仲微按法曰：“曲在浮屠。”

translations.literal: Nang Mountain Buddhist monks disputed water rights with the prefectural school; long unsettled; Zhongwei judged by law saying: "The wrong lies with the monks."
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist monks at Mount Nang and the prefectural school had disputed irrigation rights for years without resolution; Zhongwei ruled by law, "The monks are in the wrong."

sentences.zh: 它日沿檄過寺，其徒久揭其事鐘上以為冤，旦暮祝詛，然莫省為仲微也。

translations.literal: Another day traveling on commission he passed the monastery; its disciples long had posted the affair on the bell as a grievance, morning and evening praying curses, yet none recognized it was Zhongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while traveling on official business, he passed the monastery. The monks had long posted the case on the temple bell as an injustice and cursed him morning and night, not realizing their judge was passing before them.

sentences.zh: 仲微見之曰：“吾何心哉？

translations.literal: Zhongwei seeing it said: "What heart have I?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei saw it and said, "What ill will had I toward you?

sentences.zh: 吾何心哉？”

translations.literal: What heart have I?"
translations.idiomatic: What ill will had I toward you?"

sentences.zh: 質明，首僧無疾而死。

translations.literal: At dawn, the chief monk without illness died.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn the head monk had died suddenly, without any prior illness.

sentences.zh: 寓公有誦仲微於當路而密授以薦牘者，仲微受而藏之。

translations.literal: A resident gentleman praised Zhongwei to those in power and secretly handed him a recommendation document; Zhongwei received and stored it.
translations.idiomatic: A local gentleman who lodged in the county praised Zhongwei to those in power and secretly gave him a recommendation; Zhongwei accepted it and put it away.

sentences.zh: 逾年，其家負縣租，竟逮其奴。

translations.literal: After a year his household owed county rent; in the end his slave was seized.
translations.idiomatic: A year later his household fell behind on county taxes, and Zhongwei had his servant arrested.

sentences.zh: 寓公有怨言，仲微還其牘，緘封如故，其人慚謝，終其任不敢撓以私。

translations.literal: The resident gentleman had resentful words; Zhongwei returned his document, the seal as before; the man ashamed apologized; to the end of his term dared not press him with private interest.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman complained bitterly. Zhongwei returned the recommendation, still sealed as he had received it. The man apologized in shame and never again tried to sway him with private favors for the rest of his term.

sentences.zh: 遷海鹽丞。

translations.literal: Moved to Haiyan Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be assistant director of the Haiyan salt commission.

sentences.zh: 鄰邑有疑獄十年，郡命仲微按之，一問立決。

translations.literal: A neighboring county had a doubtful case ten years; the prefecture ordered Zhongwei to investigate it; one question and it was immediately decided.
translations.idiomatic: A neighboring county had a doubtful case unresolved for ten years; the prefecture ordered Zhongwei to review it, and one round of questioning settled it at once.

sentences.zh: 改知崇陽縣，寢食公署旁，日與父老樵豎相爾汝，下情畢達，吏無所措手。

translations.literal: Changed to magistrate of Chongyang County; he slept and ate beside the public office, daily with elders and woodcutters using intimate thou/you, lower sentiments fully reached, clerks had nowhere to lay hands.
translations.idiomatic: He was made magistrate of Chongyang County, lodging beside the yamen; each day he spoke familiarly with elders and woodcutters until every grievance reached him, leaving his clerks no room to meddle.

sentences.zh: 通判黃州，職兼餉饋，以身律下，隨事檢柅，軍興賴以不乏。

translations.literal: Vice prefect of Huangzhou, duties including provisioning; with his person he disciplined subordinates, along affairs inspected and restrained, military campaigns relied on this for no lack.
translations.idiomatic: As vice prefect of Huangzhou he also oversaw supply lines; he disciplined his staff by personal example, checked abuses at every turn, and the armies were kept supplied throughout the campaigns.

sentences.zh: 制置使上其最，辭曰：“職分也，何最之有？”

translations.literal: The commissioner reported his top rating; he declined saying: "It was my duty—what top rating is there?"
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner reported him for outstanding service, but he declined, saying, "I only did my duty—what merit is there in that?"

sentences.zh: 復通判江州，遷幹辦諸司審計事，知贛州、江西提點刑獄，迕丞相賈似道，監察御史舒有開言罷。

translations.literal: Again vice prefect of Jiangzhou, moved to Commissioner of Various Offices Audit Affairs, prefect of Ganzhou and Jiangxi Judicial Intendant, crossed Chief Councillor Jia Sidao; Investigating Censor Shu Youkai spoke and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He served again as vice prefect of Jiangzhou, then as commissioner of audit affairs for the various offices, and as prefect of Ganzhou and judicial intendant for Jiangxi. He offended Chief Councillor Jia Sidao; Investigating Censor Shu Youkai memorialized for his removal, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，起知惠州，遷太府寺丞兼權侍右郎官。

translations.literal: After long time, raised as prefect of Huizhou, moved to Revenue Court Assistant Director while Acting Right Attendant Service Director.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled to be prefect of Huizhou, then made assistant director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury while acting as director in the Right Service.

sentences.zh: 輪對，言：“祿餌可以釣天下之中才，而不可啖嘗天下之豪傑；

translations.literal: At audience he said: "Salary bait can fish all under Heaven's middling talents, yet cannot be tasted by all under Heaven's heroes;
translations.idiomatic: At a palace audience he said, "Stipends may hook the middling talent of the realm, but they cannot tempt its true heroes to take a bite;

sentences.zh: 名航可以載天下之猥士，而不可以陸沉天下之英雄。”

translations.literal: Fame's vessel can carry all under Heaven's base scholars, yet cannot land-sink all under Heaven's heroes."
translations.idiomatic: official titles may carry the base men of the realm, but they cannot drown its heroes in obscurity."

sentences.zh: 似道怒，又諷言者罷奪其官。

translations.literal: Sidao was angry; again through insinuation to memorializers he was dismissed and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao was enraged; through his allies he had Zhongwei dismissed again and stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 久之，敘復。

translations.literal: After long time, his rank was restored in order.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 時國勢危甚，仲微上封事，其略曰：“誤襄者，老將也。

translations.literal: At the time the state's situation was very perilous; Zhongwei submitted a sealed memorial, its gist saying: "Those who lost Xiang were the old generals.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in grave peril. Zhongwei submitted a sealed memorial whose gist ran: "Those who lost Xiangyang were the old generals.

sentences.zh: 夫襄之罪不專在於庸閫、疲將、孩兵也，君相當分受其責，以謝先皇帝在天之靈。

translations.literal: Now Xiang's guilt lies not solely in mediocre commanders, weary generals, and childish troops; ruler and chief minister ought to share in bearing the blame, to apologize to the late emperor's spirit in Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the fault at Xiangyang does not rest solely on incompetent commanders, worn-out generals, or untrained soldiers—the emperor and his chief minister must share the blame and make amends before the spirit of the late emperor in Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天子若曰罪在朕躬，大臣宜言咎在臣等，宣布十年養安之往繆，深懲六年玩寇之昨非，救過未形，固已無極，追悔既往，尚愈於迷。

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven says guilt lies on my person, great ministers ought to say fault lies on us ministers, proclaim the past errors of ten years' nurturing peace, deeply punish six years' past wrong of treating the enemy lightly, saving faults not yet formed is already without limit, repenting what is past is still better than delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Son of Heaven say, "The guilt is mine," and let his ministers say, "The fault is ours." Proclaim the errors of a decade spent nursing peace, and deeply repent six years of treating the enemy lightly. To correct faults before they take shape is best; to repent what is already done is still better than remaining lost.

sentences.zh: 或謂覆護之意多，克責之辭少；

translations.literal: Some say shielding intent is much, words of overcoming blame are few;
translations.idiomatic: Some say there is too much shielding and too little self-reproach;

sentences.zh: 或謂陛下乏哭師之誓，師相飾分過之言，甚非所以慰恤死義，祈天悔禍之道也。

translations.literal: some say Your Majesty lacks the oath of weeping for the army, the chief minister adorns words of sharing fault—very much not the way to comfort those who died for righteousness and pray Heaven to repent calamity.
translations.idiomatic: others that Your Majesty lacks a solemn vow to avenge the fallen armies, while the chief minister offers only cosmetic words of shared blame—hardly the way to comfort those who died loyal and to move Heaven to turn aside disaster.

sentences.zh: 往往代言乏知體之士，翹館鮮有識之人，吮旨茹柔，積習成痼，君道相業，兩有所虧。

translations.literal: Often those who speak for others lack men who know propriety; the drafting academy rarely has men of insight; sucking sweetness, chewing softness, accumulated habit becomes chronic illness—ruler's way and chief minister's work both suffer loss.
translations.idiomatic: Too often the drafters of edicts are men who know nothing of propriety, and the drafting academy has few men of judgment. They suck up sweetness and chew on softness until the habit is chronic—both the Way of the ruler and the work of the chief minister are diminished.

sentences.zh: 方今何時，而在廷無謀國之臣，在邊無折沖之帥。

translations.literal: What time is it now, yet at court there are no ministers who plan for the state, at the borders no commanders who break the enemy's charge.
translations.idiomatic: What season is this, when at court there is no minister who plans for the state, and on the frontier no commander who can break the enemy's charge?

sentences.zh: 監之先朝宣和未亂之前、靖康既敗之後，凡前日之日近冕旒，朱輪華轂，俯首吐心，奴顏婢膝，即今日奉賊稱臣之人也；

translations.literal: Observe the former dynasty before Xuanhe's disorder and after Jingkang's defeat: all who in former days were near the imperial crown, red wheels and splendid carriages, bowing heads pouring out hearts, slave faces maid knees—that is today's men who serve the enemy and call themselves subjects;
translations.idiomatic: Look to the previous dynasty before the Xuanhe turmoil and after the Jingkang debacle: those who once pressed close to the throne, rode in gilded carriages, bowed low and poured out their hearts, fawning like slaves and maidservants—are the very men who today serve the enemy and call themselves loyal subjects;

sentences.zh: 強力敏事，捷疾快意，即今日畔君賣國之人也。

translations.literal: Strong in force, nimble in affairs, swift and pleased at heart—that is today's men who turn from the ruler and sell the state.
translations.idiomatic: those who were forceful and quick, sharp and self-satisfied—are today's men who betray their sovereign and sell out the realm.

sentences.zh: 為國者亦何便於若人哉！

translations.literal: For one who governs the state, what convenience is there in such men!
translations.idiomatic: What advantage can such men offer to those who govern the state!

sentences.zh: 迷國者進慆憂之欺以逢其君，托國者護恥敗之局而莫敢議，當國者昧安危之機而莫之悔。

translations.literal: Those who bewilder the state advance flattery and worry's deceit to please their ruler; those who entrust the state shield shameful defeat's situation and none dare discuss; those who hold the state are blind to safety and danger's turning point and do not repent.
translations.idiomatic: Men who mislead the realm offer soothing flattery to please their lord; men entrusted with the realm cover up shameful defeats and none dare speak; men who hold power ignore the turning point between safety and peril and will not repent.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗思之，今之所少不止於兵。

translations.literal: Your servant has often pondered: what is lacking today is not only troops.
translations.idiomatic: I have often reflected that what the realm lacks today is not soldiers alone.

sentences.zh: 閫外之事，將軍制之，而一級半階，率從中出，鬥粟尺布，退有後憂，平素無權，緩急有責，或請建督，或請行邊，或請京城，創聞駭聽。

translations.literal: Matters outside the commander's gate, generals ought to control them, yet one rank or half a grade all come from the center; a peck of grain, a foot of cloth—withdrawal brings later worry; in normal times no authority, in urgency blame falls—some request establishing a commissioner, some request going to the border, some request the capital city; first hearing startles the ear.
translations.idiomatic: Field commanders ought to control affairs beyond the pass, yet every promotion and every ration comes from the center; withdraw a measure of grain or cloth and they face reprisals. They have no authority in peace but bear blame in crisis. When one asks to establish a grand commissioner, another to take the field, another to defend the capital, each proposal sounds shocking at first hearing.

sentences.zh: 因諸閫有辭於緩急之時，故廟堂不得不掩惡於敗闕之後，有謀莫展，有敗無誅，上下包羞，噤無敢議。

translations.literal: Because the various commanders have excuses in times of urgency and ease, therefore the temple hall must cover evil after defeat's gaps; there is planning yet none deploys, there is defeat yet none is punished; above and below wrap shame, silenced with none daring to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Because commanders can plead their constraints in every crisis, the court must cover up failures afterward: plans go unused, defeats go unpunished, and high and low alike swallow shame in silence, none daring to speak.

sentences.zh: 是以下至器仗甲馬，衰颯厖涼，不足以肅軍容；

translations.literal: Therefore down to weapons, armor, and horses, decayed, slack, muddled and cold, insufficient to make military appearance stern;
translations.idiomatic: Hence even weapons, armor, and horses are worn out and neglected, too poor to lend the army dignity;

sentences.zh: 壁壘堡柵，折樊駕漏，不足以當沖突之騎。

translations.literal: walls, ramparts, forts, and palisades broken, rotten, leaking, insufficient to withstand charging cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: walls, ramparts, and stockades are broken and rotting, unable to withstand a cavalry charge.

sentences.zh: 號為帥閫，名存實亡也。

translations.literal: Called commanders of the pass, the name exists but the substance is gone.
translations.idiomatic: They are called frontier commanders in name only—the title remains, but the substance is gone.

sentences.zh: 城而無兵，以城與敵；

translations.literal: To have cities yet no soldiers—is to hand the cities to the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Cities without troops mean surrendering those cities to the foe;

sentences.zh: 兵不知戰，以將與敵；

translations.literal: Soldiers who do not know battle—is to hand the generals to the enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Armies that cannot fight hand their commanders to the enemy;

sentences.zh: 將不知兵，以國與敵。

translations.literal: Generals who do not understand warfare—is to hand the state to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders ignorant of war deliver the realm itself to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 光景蹙近目睫矣！

translations.literal: The prospect is pressed close to the eyelashes!
translations.idiomatic: Disaster looms as near as the eye can see!

sentences.zh: 惟君相幡然改悟，天下事尚可為也。

translations.literal: Only if lord and chancellor abruptly change and awaken may affairs under Heaven still be undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: Only if ruler and chief minister awaken at once can the empire still be saved.

sentences.zh: 轉敗為成，在君相一念間耳。”

translations.literal: Turning defeat into success lies within a single thought of lord and chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Reversing defeat into victory rests on a single resolve from the throne and its chief minister."

sentences.zh: 乃出仲微江東提點刑獄。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongwei was dispatched as Jiangdong Judicial Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed judicial intendant for Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，遷秘書監，尋拜右正言、左司諫、殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat; soon appointed Right Direct Remonstrator, Left Remonstrance Bureau Remonstrator, and Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1275 he became Director of the Secretariat, then Right Direct Remonstrator, Left Bureau Remonstrator, and Palace Censor in succession.

sentences.zh: 益王即位海上，拜吏部尚書、給事中。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yi assumed the throne at sea, he was appointed Minister of Personnel and Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yi was enthroned on the coast, he was made Minister of Personnel and Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 厓山兵敗，走安南。

translations.literal: After defeat at Yamen, he fled to Annam.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Yamen he fled to Annam.

sentences.zh: 越四年卒，年七十有二。

translations.literal: Four years later he died, at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he died, aged seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 其子文孫與安南王族人益稷出降，向導我師南征。

translations.literal: His son Wensun and Yiji, a clansman of the king of Annam, surrendered and guided our army southward.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wensun and Yiji, a kinsman of the Annamese king, defected and led our forces on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 安南王憤，伐仲微墓，斧其棺。

translations.literal: The king of Annam, enraged, attacked Zhongwei's tomb and split his coffin with an axe.
translations.idiomatic: The Annamese king, in fury, desecrated Zhongwei's grave and hacked open his coffin.

sentences.zh: 仲微天稟篤實，雖生長富貴，而惡衣菲食，自同窶人。

translations.literal: Zhongwei was endowed with deep sincerity by nature; though raised amid wealth and rank, he wore mean clothes and ate sparing fare, making himself like a poor man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwei was naturally steadfast and sincere; though born to privilege, he dressed plainly and ate frugally, living no better than a pauper.

sentences.zh: 故能涵飫《六經》，精研理致，於諸子百家、天文、地理、醫藥、卜筮、釋老之學，靡不搜獵雲。

translations.literal: Thus he could imbibe the Six Classics and probe principle to its depths; in the teachings of the hundred schools, astronomy, geography, medicine, divination, and Buddhist and Daoist learning, nothing escaped his search and mastery.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore absorbed the Six Classics and pursued principle to its depths, ranging through the hundred schools, astronomy, geography, medicine, divination, and Buddhist and Daoist lore until he had mastered them all.

sentences.zh: 梁成大，字謙之，福州人。

translations.literal: Liang Chengda, courtesy name Qianzhi, was a man of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Chengda, styled Qianzhi, came from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Kaixi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1205.

sentences.zh: 素茍賤亡恥，作縣滿秩，諂事史彌遠家幹萬昕，昕言真德秀當擊，成大曰：“某若入臺，必能辯此事。”

translations.literal: He had long been base and shameless; when his county term ended he flattered Wan Xin, a clerk in Shi Miyuan's household. Xin said Zhen Dexiu should be attacked. Chengda said: “If I enter the Censorate, I can certainly debate this matter.”
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature servile and shameless. When his county posting ended he curried favor with Wan Xin, a clerk in Shi Miyuan's household. Xin said Zhen Dexiu ought to be struck down. Chengda replied, “If I reach the Censorate, I can surely prosecute this case.”

sentences.zh: 昕為達其語。

translations.literal: Xin conveyed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Xin relayed what he had said.

sentences.zh: 通判揚州，尋遷宗正寺簿。

translations.literal: He served as deputy prefect of Yangzhou and was soon transferred to Registrar of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He became deputy prefect of Yangzhou, then Registrar of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年冬，轉對，首言：“大佞似忠，大辯若訥，或好名以自鬻，或立異以自詭，或假高尚之節以要君，或飾矯偽之學以欺世。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Baoqing, at audience he spoke first: “Great villains resemble the loyal; great eloquence seems dull. Some peddle reputation for self-sale; some pose as unconventional for self-deception; some feign lofty integrity to court the ruler; some adorn hypocritical learning to deceive the world.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 1225, at his audience he led with: “Great villains wear the mask of loyalty; glib tongues pass for reticence. Some hawk their reputations; some affect eccentricity to mystify others; some counterfeit lofty integrity to win the throne's ear; some dress up false learning to fool the age.

sentences.zh: 言若忠鯁，心實回邪，一不察焉，薰蕕同器，涇、渭雜流矣。

translations.literal: Their words seem loyal and blunt, yet their hearts are truly perverse. If one fails to examine them, fragrant and foul share one vessel, and the Jing and Wei mingle in one stream.
translations.idiomatic: They speak as though bluntly loyal while their hearts are crooked. Fail to scrutinize them, and sweet grass and stench share one jar, the Jing and Wei run together.

sentences.zh: 言不達變，謀不中機，或巧辯以為能，或詭訐以市直，或設奇險之說以駴眾聽，或肆妄誕之論以惑士心。

translations.literal: Their words do not reach change; their plans do not hit the moment. Some take clever debate for ability; some take crafty accusation for uprightness; some set forth perilous doctrines to confuse public hearing; some unleash reckless absurdities to bewilder scholars' minds.
translations.idiomatic: Their speech misses the shifting moment; their schemes miss the mark. Some parade clever argument as talent; some cloak slander as integrity; some spin dangerous theories to dazzle the crowd; some pour forth wild nonsense to unsettle the minds of the learned.

sentences.zh: 所行非所言，所守非所學，一不辯焉，枘鑿不侔，矛盾相激矣。”

translations.literal: What they do is not what they say; what they uphold is not what they study. If one fails to distinguish them, tenon and mortise do not fit, and contradictions clash against one another.
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds belie their words; their conduct betrays their learning. Leave them undistinguished, and peg and socket never meet—only contradiction and collision."

sentences.zh: 越六日，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Six days later he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Six days later he was made Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 尋奏：“魏了翁已從追竄，人猶以為罪大罰輕。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized: “Wei Liaoweng has already been pursued into exile, yet people still think the crime great and the punishment light.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted: “Wei Liaoweng has already been driven into exile, yet many still deem his crime grave and his punishment light.

sentences.zh: 真德秀狂僭悖繆，不減了翁，相羊家食，宜削秩貶竄，一等施行。”

translations.literal: Zhen Dexiu is wildly presumptuous and rebelliously perverse, no less than Liaoweng. He idles at home on salary. His rank should be stripped and he banished—the same measure applied alike.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Dexiu is insolent and perverse, no less than Liaoweng, loafing at home on state stipend. Strip his rank and banish him—apply the same penalty in full.”

sentences.zh: 章既上，不下者兩月，或傳德秀有衡陽之命，時宰於帝前及之。

translations.literal: Once the memorial was submitted, it was not acted on for two months. Rumor spread that Dexiu had an appointment to Hengyang. The chief minister mentioned it before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial sat unanswered two months. Word spread that Dexiu was to be sent to Hengyang. The chief minister raised it before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：“仲尼不為已甚。”

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Confucius did not go to excess.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “Confucius would not press a matter too far.”

sentences.zh: 遂止鐫三秩。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped at stripping three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The punishment was limited to stripping three ranks.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，又奏楊長孺寢新命，徐瑄追三秩移象州居住，胡夢昱移欽州編管。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year he again memorialized: suspend Yang Changru's new appointment; strip Xu Xuan of three ranks and move him to reside at Xiangzhou; transfer Hu Mengyu to supervised banishment at Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next March he again urged that Yang Changru's new appointment be shelved, Xu Xuan be stripped of three ranks and sent to live at Xiangzhou, and Hu Mengyu be placed under supervised banishment at Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 是冬，拜右正言。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed Right Direct Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he became Right Direct Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，進左司諫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Bureau Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In 1228 he was promoted to Left Bureau Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，遷宗正少卿。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he became Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，權刑部侍郎，明年十月，帝夜降旨黜之，提舉千秋鴻禧觀。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year he acted as Vice Minister of Justice; in the tenth month of the next year the emperor issued a night edict dismissing him to superintendent of the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year he served as acting Vice Minister of Justice; the following tenth month the emperor dismissed him by night edict and made him superintendent of the Qianqiu Hongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 莫澤時兼給事中，急於別異，上疏駁之，遂寢祠命。

translations.literal: Mo Ze was then also Supervising Secretary and, eager to distinguish himself, submitted a memorial to rebut it; the abbey appointment was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Ze, then also Supervising Secretary, eager to set himself apart, memorialized in rebuttal, and the abbey appointment was shelved.

sentences.zh: 端平初，洪咨夔、吳泳交章論駁，鐫兩秩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping, Hong Zikui and Wu Yong submitted alternating memorials of rebuttal, and two ranks were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duanping era, Hong Zikui and Wu Yong filed successive memorials against him, and two ranks were stripped.

sentences.zh: 泳復上疏，送泉州居住。

translations.literal: Yong again submitted a memorial, and he was sent to reside at Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized again, and he was ordered to live at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會王遂論亦上，再鐫秩，徙潮州。

translations.literal: When Wang Sui's critique also went up, another rank was stripped and he was moved to Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sui's critique followed, another rank was stripped and he was banished to Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 成大天資暴狠，心術崄巇，凡可賊忠害良者，率多攘臂為之。

translations.literal: Chengda was violent and fierce by nature, treacherous in mind; whatever could harm the loyal and injure the good, he mostly rolled up his sleeves to do.
translations.idiomatic: Chengda was by nature brutal and ruthless, his scheming treacherous; he eagerly took up any work that could wound the loyal and destroy the worthy.

sentences.zh: 四方賂遺，列置堂廡，賓至則導之使觀，欲其效尤也。

translations.literal: Bribes from the four quarters were arrayed in the halls and corridors; when guests arrived he guided them to look, wishing them to follow his example.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts from every quarter lined his halls; when guests came he led them on a tour, inviting them to imitate his ways.

sentences.zh: 尤嗜豪奪，冒占宇文氏賜第。

translations.literal: He was especially addicted to violent seizure and usurped the Yuwen family's granted mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially fond of seizing property by force and occupied the Yuwen family's imperial grant.

sentences.zh: 既擯歸，訟之者不下百數。

translations.literal: Once he was driven out and returned, those who sued him were no fewer than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: After he was cast out and sent home, more than a hundred people brought suit against him.

sentences.zh: 竄之日，朝命毀其廬，雖小人如李知孝亦曰：“所不堪者，他日與成大同傳耳。”

translations.literal: On the day of his banishment the court ordered his buildings destroyed. Even a petty man like Li Zhixiao said: "What one cannot bear is that someday one will share a biography with Chengda."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his exile the court ordered his house demolished. Even a scoundrel like Li Zhixiao remarked, "What I cannot stomach is ending up in the same biography as Chengda one day."

sentences.zh: 李知孝，字孝章，參知政事光之孫。

translations.literal: Li Zhixiao, courtesy name Xiaozhang, was grandson of the Vice Grand Councillor Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhixiao, styled Xiaozhang, was grandson of Vice Grand Councillor Li Guang.

sentences.zh: 嘉定四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in 1211.

sentences.zh: 嘗為右丞相府主管文字，不以為恥。

translations.literal: He once served as chief clerk of documents in the Right Chancellor's office and did not regard it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as chief document clerk in the Right Chancellor's office and felt no shame in it.

sentences.zh: 差充幹辦諸司審計司，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was detailed as clerk of the Bureau for Auditing the Various Offices and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as clerk of the Bureau for Auditing the Various Offices, then appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 寶慶元年八月，上疏：“士大夫汲汲好名，正救之力少而附和沽激之意多，扶持之意微而詆訾扇搖之意勝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Baoqing he submitted a memorial: “Scholar-officials hurry to seek reputation. The force of upright rescue is slight, while the intent to echo and trade in excitement is great. The intent to support is faint, while the intent to slander and fan unrest prevails.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1225 he memorialized: “The literati scramble for fame. Few truly work to rescue the state; many rush to echo sensational posturing. Support for sound policy is weak; slander and agitation carry the day.

sentences.zh: 既慮君上之或不能用，又恐朝廷之或不能容，姑為激怒之辭，退俟斥逐之命。

translations.literal: They fear the ruler may not employ them, yet also fear the court may not tolerate them. For the moment they utter words to provoke anger, then withdraw to await orders of dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the sovereign may not use them, yet also fearing the court may not tolerate them, they first speak words meant to provoke, then withdraw to await expulsion.

sentences.zh: 始則慷慨而激烈，終則懇切而求去，將以樹奇節而求令名，此臣之所未解。”

translations.literal: At first they are ardent and fierce; in the end they earnestly beg to leave—intending to plant extraordinary integrity and seek a fine name. This is what your servant does not understand.”
translations.idiomatic: They begin in bold indignation and end by pleading to resign, all to cultivate a reputation for singular integrity. That is what your servant cannot fathom.”

sentences.zh: 蓋陰詆真德秀等。

translations.literal: This was in secret to slander Zhen Dexiu and others.
translations.idiomatic: The attack was aimed covertly at Zhen Dexiu and his circle.

sentences.zh: 又奏洪咨夔鐫三秩、放罷，胡夢昱追毀、除名、勒停，羈管象州。

translations.literal: He again memorialized that Hong Zikui should be stripped of three ranks and dismissed; Hu Mengyu should have honors revoked retroactively, be removed from the rolls, compelled to cease office, and placed under supervised banishment at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged stripping Hong Zikui of three ranks and dismissing him; Hu Mengyu should have his honors revoked, be struck from the rolls, barred from office, and placed under supervised exile at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 知孝猶語魏了翁曰：“此所論咨夔等，乃府第付出全文。”

translations.literal: Zhixiao still told Wei Liaoweng: “This memorial concerning Zikui and the rest was the full text issued from the chief minister's residence.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiao even told Wei Liaoweng, “The memorial against Zikui and the others was the full text handed down from the chief minister's residence.”

sentences.zh: 其情狀變詐如此。

translations.literal: His conduct of deceit and shift was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the deceit and double-dealing of his conduct.

sentences.zh: 越月，復言：“近年以來，諸老雕零，後學晚出，不見前輩，不聞義理，不講綱常，識見卑陋，議論偏诐，更唱叠和，蠱惑人心，此風披扇，為害實深。

translations.literal: A month later he spoke again: “In recent years the elders have withered away; later students emerge late. They do not see former generations, do not hear of principle and reason, do not discuss the constants. Their insight is base and crude; their discourse biased and crooked. They answer one another in chorus, bewitching people's hearts. This wind spreads wide; the harm is truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he spoke again: “In recent years the old masters have passed away and younger scholars come late to learning. They never met the elders, never heard true principle, never studied the moral constants. Their vision is shallow, their talk partisan. They echo one another in chorus, poisoning minds. The fashion spreads; the damage runs deep.

sentences.zh: 乞下臣章，風厲內外，各務靖共，以杜亂萌。”

translations.literal: I beg that your servant's memorial be issued, to admonish within and without, that each may devote himself to quiet accord and cut off the sprout of disorder.”
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this memorial be promulgated to admonish the court and the realm, that all may pursue harmony and nip disorder in the bud.”

sentences.zh: 拜右正言。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Direct Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Direct Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 又言：“德秀節改聖語，繆謄牒示，導信邪說，簧鼓同流，其或再有妄言，當追削流竄，以正典刑。”

translations.literal: He also said: “Dexiu alters the sage's words section by section, falsely copies and displays documents, leads people to trust heterodox doctrines, and drums the same current with a reed. If he again utters reckless words, he should be pursued, stripped, and banished in exile to rectify the statutory punishment.”
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “Dexiu edits the sage's words line by line, copies and displays false documents, spreads heterodox teaching, and drums his faction onward. Should he speak recklessly again, strip his honors, pursue him, and exile him to uphold the law.”

sentences.zh: 疏既上，遂鏤榜播告天下。

translations.literal: Once the memorial was submitted, a carved placard was then proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial was in, an engraved proclamation was broadcast across the empire.

sentences.zh: 又言：“趣召之人，率皆遲回，久而不至，以要君為高致，以共命為常流，可行而固不行，不疾而稱有疾，比比皆是，相扇成風，欲求難進易退之名，殊失尊君親上之義。

translations.literal: He also said: “Those urgently summoned mostly delay and linger, long failing to arrive—taking pressing the ruler as lofty conduct, taking shared command as the common current. They could go yet firmly do not; they are not ill yet claim illness. Such cases are everywhere, fanning one another into a wind, seeking the name of hard to advance and easy to withdraw—utterly losing the meaning of honoring the ruler and cleaving to superiors.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “Men urgently summoned mostly linger and never come, treating defiance of the throne as lofty conduct and routine delay as normal. Able to serve, they refuse; not ill, they plead sickness. Examples abound, each encouraging the next, all chasing the fame of being hard to summon and quick to quit—betraying the duty to honor the sovereign and the court.

sentences.zh: 願將趣召之人計其程途，限以時日，使之造朝；

translations.literal: I wish that for those urgently summoned their route be calculated and a time limit set, so that they may come to court;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that for each urgently summoned man his route be reckoned and a deadline set, compelling him to appear at court;

sentences.zh: 其有衰病者，早與改命。”

translations.literal: for those who are aged and ill, let a new appointment be given early.”
translations.idiomatic: and for those truly aged or ill, let a new appointment be granted promptly.”

sentences.zh: 時召傅伯成、楊簡、劉宰等皆不至，故知孝詆之。

translations.literal: At the time Fu Bocheng, Yang Jian, Liu Zai, and others had all been summoned yet did not come; therefore Zhixiao slandered them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bocheng, Yang Jian, Liu Zai, and others had been summoned but did not come—hence Zhixiao's attack.

sentences.zh: 又奏張忠恕落職、鐫秩、罷郡。

translations.literal: He again memorialized that Zhang Zhongshu should be removed from office, stripped of rank, and dismissed from his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that Zhang Zhongshu be removed from office, stripped of rank, and dismissed from his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知孝拜殿中侍御史，升侍御史。

translations.literal: Zhixiao was appointed Palace Censor and promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiao became Palace Censor, then Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年，遷右司諫，進右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoding he was transferred to Right Remonstrance Bureau Remonstrator and advanced to Right Remonstrance and Policy Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In 1228 he became Right Bureau Remonstrator, then Right Remonstrance and Policy Grandee.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷工部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Minister of Works with concurrent appointment as Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Minister of Works and Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 越月，進兵部。

translations.literal: A month later he was advanced to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he became Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，理宗親政，以寶謨閣直學士出知寧國，後省駁之，令提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: The next year, when Emperor Lizong took personal rule, he was sent out as Academician Expositor-in-Waiting of the Baomo Pavilion to govern Ningguo; the Secretariat rebutted it and ordered him to superintendent of the Songshan Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Emperor Lizong assumed personal rule, he was sent out as Baomo Pavilion academician to govern Ningguo; the Secretariat blocked the appointment and made him superintendent of the Songshan Chongfu Palace instead.

sentences.zh: 端平初，監察御史洪咨夔、權直舍人院吳泳交章論駁，鐫秩罷祠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duanping, Investigating Censor Hong Zikui and Acting Attendant of the Academy Wu Yong submitted alternating memorials of rebuttal; his rank was stripped and his abbey post ended.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duanping era, Investigating Censor Hong Zikui and Acting Academy Attendant Wu Yong filed successive memorials against him; his rank was stripped and his sinecure revoked.

sentences.zh: 泳復封駁，繼送婺州居住。

translations.literal: Yong again sealed a rebuttal, and he was then sent to reside at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sealed another rebuttal, and he was ordered to live at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史王遂且論之，再鐫秩，徙瑞州。

translations.literal: Palace Censor Wang Sui also criticized him; another rank was stripped and he was moved to Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Censor Wang Sui joined the attack; another rank was stripped and he was banished to Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 知孝起自名家，茍於仕進，領袖庶頑，懷諼迷國，排斥諸賢殆盡。

translations.literal: Zhixiao rose from a famous house yet was shameless in seeking advancement, leading the base and obstinate, harboring flattery that bewildered the state, and driving out nearly all the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Though born to a distinguished house, Zhixiao was shameless in climbing the ladder, leading the vulgar and obstinate, flattering his way into confusion of state affairs, and hounding nearly every worthy man from office.

sentences.zh: 時乘小輿，謁醉從官之家，侵欲斂積，不知紀極。

translations.literal: At the time he rode in a small carriage to visit the homes of drunken attendants, encroaching and amassing without knowing any limit.
translations.idiomatic: He would ride in a small carriage to the houses of drunken retainers, grasping and hoarding without limit.

sentences.zh: 紹定末，猶自乞為中丞，世指知孝及梁成大、莫澤為三兇。

translations.literal: Late in Shaoding he still begged to become Censor-in-Chief. The age pointed to Zhixiao together with Liang Chengda and Mo Ze as the Three Villains.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Shaoding era he still petitioned to become Censor-in-Chief. The world named Zhixiao, Liang Chengda, and Mo Ze the Three Villains.

sentences.zh: 卒以貶死，天下快之。

translations.literal: In the end he died in banishment, and all under Heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: He died in exile at last, to the relief of the realm.

sentences.zh: 論曰：讀《本政書》，然後知林勛之於井地，可謂密矣。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: Read the Ben Zheng Shu, and then one knows that Lin Xun on the well-field system may be called thorough.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Only after reading the Ben Zheng Shu does one see how thorough Lin Xun's treatment of the well-field system truly was.

sentences.zh: 劉才邵能全名節於權奸之時。

translations.literal: Liu Caishao could preserve his reputation and integrity in the time of powerful villains.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Caishao preserved his integrity even under powerful villains.

sentences.zh: 許忻之論和議，最為忠懇，卒以是去國，尤足悲夫。

translations.literal: Xu Xin's discourse on the peace talks was most loyal and earnest; in the end he left the state for it—especially enough to grieve one.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xin's argument on the peace negotiations was the most loyal and earnest; he left office for it in the end—a tragedy indeed.

sentences.zh: 應孟明、曾三聘之不汙韓侂胄，孔子所謂“歲寒然後知松柏之後雕也”。

translations.literal: Ying Mengming and Zeng Sanpin's not being stained by Han Tuozhou are what Confucius called “Only after the year grows cold does one know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither.”
translations.idiomatic: That Ying Mengming and Zeng Sanpin were not stained by Han Tuozhou is what Confucius meant when he said, “Only when the year turns cold do we see that pine and cypress wither last.”

sentences.zh: 徐僑之清節，度正之淳敏，牛大年之廉正，陳仲微之忠實，然皆不至於大用，非可惜哉！

translations.literal: Xu Qiao's pure integrity, Du Zheng's honest quickness, Niu Danian's clean uprightness, Chen Zhongwei's loyal steadfastness—yet none reached great employment. Is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qiao's purity, Du Zheng's sincere acuity, Niu Danian's integrity, Chen Zhongwei's loyal steadfastness—yet none was employed to the full. How regrettable!

sentences.zh: 若乃程必之竊取富貴，梁成大、李知孝甘為史彌遠鷹犬，遺臭萬年者也。

translations.literal: As for Cheng Bi's usurping wealth and rank, and Liang Chengda and Li Zhixiao's willingly serving as Shi Miyuan's hawk and hound—they are those who leave a stench for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: As for Cheng Bi, who stole wealth and rank, and Liang Chengda and Li Zhixiao, who gladly served as Shi Miyuan's hawks and hounds—their infamy will endure ten thousand years.
